#1876. Dominik Szoboszlai upsets Bradley Barcola: Four things you may have missed from Liverpool vs Club Brugge

Correspondent AUTHORITY Football journalist with experience at Reach PLC and PA Media; University of Central Lancashire graduate. FOCUS Fan-engagement content and match analysis across the Premier League and Championship. THE INSIGHT Oliver utilises a network of club and industry contacts to deliver verified reporting and fan-first content. He provides the human stories behind the results to ensure fans get the full picture as it happens.

Dominik Szoboszlai made a clear mistake despite Liverpool's 3-0 win over Club Brugge in the Champions League.

The Reds took an early lead as Alexander Isak continued his strong start to the season by tapping home Szoboszlai’s pass across the box.

Florian Wirtz doubled the visitors' lead 11 minutes from time with a superb strike before Isak grabbed his brace.

Liverpool are now fifth in the Champions League table with four wins from their first five league stage games.

The game was action-packed as Brugge gave a good account of themselves both on and off the pitch.

Football Insider have picked out four things that even the most eagle-eyed fans may not have spotted from the Reds' win in Belgium.

Many rousing renditions of Liverpool's anthem have preceded iconic and poignant Champions League nights at Anfield, hence why it is known worldwide.

The majority of genuine football fans will also know that the likes of Celtic and Borussia Dortmund have adopted the Gerry & The Pacemakers tune.

You’ll Never Walk Alone being sung by both sets of supporters pic.twitter.com/6E2fQWtZbv

Yet some may not know that Club Brugge fans also sing it before their home games, and so the travelling Reds supporters were able to join in as it blared through the speakers ahead of kick-off in Belgium.

Szoboszlai has come in for some criticism among Liverpool fans, and it was easy to understand why based on this showing.

Not only did he struggle to impact proceedings after assisting Isak's first, the Hungarian also stopped teammate Barcola scoring in the 76th minute.

The French forward looked for all the world like he was about to slot home after driving into the box with the ball, but Szoboszlai, whose open-play work in the final third is hit-and-miss, ran across his path just as he shaped to shoot with his left foot.

An incredible moment that ultimately led to Brugge coming away with the ball with ease.

Barcola did little to hide his anguish as he made his frustration plain at his Liverpool teammate.

Neutral viewers could be forgiven for thinking that they were looking at the away fans as large sections of the Jan Breydelstadion were draped in Union Jack flags.

It was not Liverpool's doing, however, with home supporters initially using the flag as part of a pre-match tifo display, along with the slogan: “Founded by Brits, rooted in Flemish soil."

The use of the flags throughout the game and around the ground comes from the club being founded by Brits, and also dates back to the 1970s, when Brugge played two European finals at Wembley against Liverpool and their fans were inspired by the atmosphere created by the Merseyside natives on both occasions.

Isak has now scored in six consecutive away appearances, with previous strikes against Crystal Palace, Fenerbahce, Brentford, Bournemouth and Ipswich Town.

He joined a list of just seven other club greats who have done the same in Bruges, with those being Dick Forshaw, Sam English, Gordon Hodgson, John Evans, John Aldridge, John Barnes and Mo Salah.

Salah is the only other Reds star to have done so in the Premier League era, and Isak will be keen to equal his club-record of seven in a row away from home this weekend against rivals Everton.

#1872. 'If they don't win, it could bankrupt them' - Expert reacts to Man City appeal update

The Premier League could be bankrupted by the financial and legal nightmare that will follow if Manchester City win their appeal.

That is according to experienced former Tottenham, Aston Villa and Everton scout, Bryan King, speaking exclusively to Football Insider.

The Citizens were found guilty of 114 breaches of the Premier League's financial rules by a independent commission in September, almost two years after the hearing ended and nearly four years since the charges were announced.

Man City's appeal is expected to be heard next month, with potential sanctions to come next year if it fails.

There has been talk of legal action towards the Premier League, too, which could in the aftermath of the eventual decision.

But last week, Premier League clubs voted to cover the board's legal costs if Man City's sponsors do decide to pursue legal action in a personal capacity.

Clubs have agreed to cover the Premier League board’s legal costs if Manchester City’s sponsors decide to sue them in a personal capacity.At a meeting of club owners and executives in London on Thursday — their first gathering since the judgment against City was announced in…

Whatever way the decision ultimately goes, fans of every Premier League club will eventually be glad to see the back of Man City's case.

The charges have been a constant talking point for nearly four years and for some, has tainted the competition.

"I tell you what, if the Premier League don't win it, it could bankrupt them," King told Football Insider. "Can you imagine the money it's cost?

"Again, are they all going to put the same amount of money to cover it [the Premier League's legal fees]? Or is there going to be a scaling system of the big six and the rest?

"Again, the whole thing at the end of the day has become a farcical situation. If you're guilty on 114 charges, even if 113 aren't proven and one is, then accept your punishment and give them punishment.

"Because it doesn't matter whether it's 114 guilty or one guilty. They all relate to the same thing anyway. Money."

Immediately after the first verdict emerged, Man City beat Liverpool 3-0 at Anfield in a show of defiance.

They then beat Ipswich Town, winning all seven of their opening Premier League games and looking stronger than ever.

Since then, Enzo Maresca's have lost to Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest, and drew with Fulham on Saturday to make it four games without a win.

There will be a dark cloud hanging over Man City all the while an outcome of their appeal is yet to come.

#1866. Serie A preview: AC Milan vs. Frosinone – Team news, opposition insight, stats and prediction

Milan will return to action on Sunday evening, hoping to pick up where they left off before the international break with a strong performance against Frosinone.

If we look at the league, it has been a very decent start to the season for Ruben Amorim and his men. However, they are yet to win three games on the trot, so tomorrow’s encounter is a fantastic chance for them to really show their worth.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It won’t be easy, though. Amorim said during his press conference that it’s hard to identify the movement patterns of Frosinone, who certainly have the ability to make life difficult for the Rossoneri.

Game date: Sunday, November 22 Kick-off time: 18:00 (CET) Venue: San Siro Referee: Luca Pairetto (VAR: Pezzuto)

Some good news arrived on Saturday morning as Strahinja Pavlovic was deemed fit enough to be called up for the game. It’s not certain whether he will start or not, but Amorim at least said that he’s happy to have the Serbian and ‘his fire’ back.

A few days ago, it was also confirmed that Mike Maignan will be at the manager’s disposal despite the injury scare with France. Of course, it’s not all perfect on the injury front as Matteo Gabbia, Fikayo Tomori, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Alexis Saelemaekers and Samuel Chukwueze are still sidelined.

Anyway, moving on to the predicted starting eleven, it was initially thought that Amorim would field the same one as we saw against Genoa. However, he made it very clear during the presser that Musah won’t play as a left-back, so there will indeed be some changes.

According to the latest reports, the American will still start but in midfield instead, allowing Adrien Rabiot to have a slightly more advanced role. It also means that Davide Bartesaghi will come into the eleven, currently ahead of Pervis Estupinan in the race.

Alphadjo Cisse has been in red-hot form lately but it seems Amorim wants to manage expectations a little, with the youngster tipped to start on the bench. Christian Pulisic should thus have a role on the flank as opposed to in the centre, although one would imagine everything will be a bit fluid.

It’s no surprise to see that Goncalo Ramos should start up front, but of course, he will need to get going with the goalscoring sooner rather than later. Francesco Camarda is knocking on the door, as is Cisse who has been tested in that role before.

Predicted Milan XI (4-3-3): Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Diawara, Bartesaghi; Musah, Modric, Rabiot; Moreira, Ramos, Pulisic.

Predicted bench: Torriani, P. Terracciano, F. Terracciano, Pavlovic, Vladimirov, Estupinan, Jashari, Comotto, Hutchinson, Cisse, Camarda.

Injuries & suspensions: Gabbia, Tomori, Loftus-Cheek, Saelemaekers and Chukwueze.

Frosinone have definitely been one of the surprises of the season so far. After a very strong Serie B campaign with 81 points and only three games lost, they secured direct promotion to the top tier (finishing second) and have been making the most of the adventure.

They are currently on 20 points after eleven games, winning six, drawing two and losing three, which has put them in sixth place. That’s very strong for a newcomer and for a coach who is only in his second season with the club, especially considering the upset against Como.

It’s the 56-year-old’s second attempt at Serie A after coaching Cremonese for half a season in 2022-23. He didn’t manage a single win then, so you can definitely say that the performance so far has been great revenge for him.

So, what is behind this rise? As pointed out by Gazzetta dello Sport, the direct style of play has been key for Frosinone. As opposed to Milan, who want to see a lot of the ball, they are willing to have less possession and break on the counter.

It doesn’t mean that they sit back, though. In fact, it has been the opposite as they are the highest-pressing team in the league. The strategy thus seems to be to force mistakes out of the opponents, while also making sure that they are direct in possession.

While collective effort deserves most of the praise, it has definitely helped that the likes of Giacomo Calo, Giorgi Kvernadze and Antonio Raimondo – among others – have performed at a very high level. They aren’t exactly big-name players, so a lot of them are having their breakout seasons.

Moving on to actual team news, the situation up front is not ideal for Frosinone as their top scorer, the aforementioned Antonio Raimondo, is out injured. Birigilea, who is on two goals, is set to replace him in the No.9 position.

The Milan academy product Sebastiano Desplanches, who left the club four years ago, will be on the bench. He’s yet to make an appearance this season, with Alvini preferring Lorenzo Palmisani instead.

Predicted Frosinone XI (4-2-3-1): Palmisani; Oyono, Calvani, Monterisi, Terzic; Calo, Masini; Ghedjemis; Schmid, Kvernadze; Birigilea.

Predicted bench: Desplanches, Pisseri, Cittadini, Tchato, Amey, Akpoguma, Fayed, El Azzouzi, Cichella, Hasa, Fini, Zerbin, Bobcek.

Injuries & suspensions: Bracaglia, Grillitsch and Raimondo.

This fixture has only been played six times, but even with such a small sample size, it’s clear that Milan are the favourites with four wins and two draws so far. They have won the last three as well, spread across the 2023-24 and 2018-19 seasons.

That said, the most recent encounter was a dramatic one, if you like. Olivier Giroud opened the scoring for Milan away from home but then Frosinone scored twice. Thanks to goals from Matteo Gabbia and Luka Jovic, the Rossoneri were able to turn it back in their favour.

The last time at San Siro, meanwhile, it was a great 3-1 win as Jovic, Pulisic and Tomori found the back of the net. Most of you will remember the American’s goal, as it was Maignan who assisted him with a fantastic pass.

➤ Milan are unbeaten in all six previous meetings against Frosinone in Serie A (W4 D2): among the teams against which they have never lost in the competition, the Rossoneri have played more games only against Pisa (14 – six also against Crotone and Lecco).

➤ Milan have scored at least three goals in four of their six Serie A matches against Frosinone, producing 15 goals overall, an average of 2.5 per game. Only against Pescara (2.9) have they recorded a higher average, among the opponents they have faced on at least five occasions (2.5 also against Casale and Messina).

➤ Frosinone have won six games this season, drawing two and losing three. Only three newly promoted teams in the last 40 years have recorded more wins in their first 12 Serie A games of the season: Bari in 1994/95 (seven), Chievo in 2001/02 (seven), and Hellas Verona in 2013/14 (seven).

➤ Milan have won four of their last five league games (L1), scoring at least two goals in each, after failing to win three of their previous four (D3). The last time they scored more than one goal in consecutive Serie A matches was between September 2020 and January 2021, when they managed 15 games.

➤ Although Frosinone are unbeaten in three of their five away games this season (W1 D2), they have won just two of their last 27 away games in Serie A (including previous participations), with 10 draws and 15 defeats.

➤ Milan have failed to win four of their last seven Serie A games played after the international break (D2 L2). On the other hand, Frosinone are unbeaten in three of their last five top-flight matches immediately following Italy matches (W2 D1).

➤ Frosinone have attempted the most counterattacks from advantageous situations in Serie A this season: 22, almost double the number of any other team. On the other hand, Milan are the only team that haven’t allowed a single counterattack when trailing in the current campaign.

➤ Only Juventus (79) have attempted more long-range shots than Frosinone (77) this season. On the other hand, Milan are the team that have attempted the fewest shots from outside the area (30) and the one that have conceded the most shots from outside the area in relation to the total conceded, 44%.

➤ Adrien Rabiot has earned the most points for his team from direct goal contributions this season, having scored 10 goals and assisted four times. In the most recent matchday, he became the first Milan midfielder to be involved in at least one goal in six consecutive league appearances since Kaká in 2004 (who managed seven).

➤ Only Matías Soulé (80) has been involved in more sequences ending with a shot than Giacomo Calò (76) in this Serie A. The Frosinone player has scored five goals in the current campaign and only one midfielder has scored more goals in the first 12 matchdays in the top flight for a newly promoted team in the three points for a win era: Hidetoshi Nakata with Perugia in 1998/99 (six).

Since Frosinone like to play on the counterattacks, one player who I think could be crucial for Milan is Musah. As he’s set to start in midfield and not at left-back, the feeling is that his main role will be to prevent the opponents from having too much open space on the counter.

Further up the pitch, I’m excited to see Moreira. He got himself a goal in Belgium’s win over Italy and he has looked a lot better on the right flank ever since the derby performance. He can definitely make the difference with his skill.

As for Frosinone, it’s obvious that Calo is the man whom Milan will want to stop. He likes to dictate the play and if he’s allowed too much time on the ball, identifying his teammates in good positions, then there could be trouble for the Rossoneri.

It will also be interesting to see if Birigilea can fill the shoes of Raimondo. He bagged a brace against Lecce but in the last two games, he failed to find the back of the net. He will surely be keen to get back on target.

A lot of people are expecting this to be a high-scoring affair and that’s a very reasonable take, given how both teams play. That said, I think this could be one where Milan actually get their defence in order and don’t concede, even if that might be a somewhat optimistic prediction.

#1865. Mac Allister not so sad now after Liverpool comeback winner

Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under new head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.

On the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness. Sadness that, unlike fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai – Liverpool’s other scorer here – and Ryan Gravenberch, he had not been offered and signed a new contract.

So, earn it. And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him. He scored with an arresting second-half shot, which proved to be the winner, and the smile across his face said it all. Not so sad now as he was later substituted to a standing ovation with Gravenberch taking his place.

The goal came early in the second half, with Iraola attributing that to adjusting his tactics after being flummoxed by Atlético’s back five and packed midfield in a first half when Liverpool were second best.

Mac Allister was heavily involved through the build-up, eventually picking out Rio Ngumoha on the left whose shot was blocked and pinballed around. It dropped to Mac Allister, 20 yards out, and he hit the kind of unerring drive that gives the goalkeeper no chance. And so it proved. Boom. And Anfield was bouncing.

Mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W

There are certainly signs under Iraola, and following a difficult last campaign, that Mac Allister is beginning to rediscover the form he showed during his first two seasons at Liverpool. Time and again the 27-year-old made vital interventions, showed aggression and walked the tightrope of a harsh early yellow card. He dovetailed with Szoboszlai and that might be a concern for Gravenberch – watched by the Netherlands’ new head coach Xavi Hernández – if Iraola persists with this approach.

Although Mac Allister has two years left on his current deal, the last thing Liverpool need is yet another attention-sapping contract saga, even if he is not the same scale of player as Mohamed Salah or Trent Alexander-Arnold.

For Iraola, after three Premier League games, comprising two draws and a victory over newly-promoted Ipswich Town, this will hopefully be lift off. A big European night at Anfield and coming from behind to beat one of the continent’s heavyweights.

“I loved it,” Iraola said, before castigating himself for misreading the way Atlético would line up. And what of Mac Allister’s riposte? There was a smile from Iraola before the Spaniard’s usual diplomacy kicked in as he talked about a “lovely, lovely goal” and how good it was for his midfielders to contribute.

Liverpool had to fight for it and what will have satisfied Iraola is that the defence, which has come under such scrutiny, held out. Even so, there are still serious concerns over the suitability of Milos Kerkez at left-back – who was badly at fault for Atlético’s goal – although the robust Ronald Araújo showed he can be a strong and versatile option on the other flank. The Uruguayan, signed on loan from Barcelona, is such a presence in both penalty areas and has the capacity to gain cult status.

As does £123m signing from Paris St-Germain Bradley Barcola, who should have scored – once, certainly, possibly twice – and possesses astonishing pace that will undoubtedly lead to goals. There are also encouraging signs that his presence could enliven Florian Wirtz. Barcola eventually also went off, but thankfully it was only to cramp.

There was a collective intake of breath across the Kop when Marcos Llorente was played through and bore down on them to give Atlético the lead. There was a desperate hope that he had strayed offside. There was then a realisation that Kerkez had, however, played him on with an appalling lack of awareness. Llorente beat Alisson.

It owed much to a wonderful shimmy, deceiving Szoboszlai in centre field, by Julián Alvarez before he smartly threaded the ball through, and Mac Allister’s international team-mate almost doubled Atlético’s advantage soon after. Only to be denied by Alisson.

Llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc

We knew, we feared it would be Llorente who scored. Remarkably, he has now half of his 10 goals in this competition against Liverpool. Indeed, he named his dog Anfield after his extra-time brace knocked Liverpool, then the holders, out in the last 16 in 2020. And Liverpool had made a dog’s dinner of defending this time.

This is a different Atlético. A far less defensive, far more expansive Atlético. In years gone by, once they were 1-0 it was game over under Diego Simeone. But these days they try and play more and that gives their opponents a chance. And so it proved.

Atlético goalkeeper Jan Oblak did well to deny Barcola, with his trailing foot, before Wirtz won the ball back and found Szoboszlai who eventually ended the movement. It owed much, however, to a clever backheel to pick out the midfielder who finished low into the corner. Who executed that backheel? That would be Araújo.

Szoboszlai slots home after a brilliant flick from Araujo! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrHQTwtgsY

Barcola should have scored, sent clear by Wirtz in a brilliant, sweeping counter-attack, before Mac Allister did.

The question now was whether Liverpool would show the resilience to see through the result. As Iraola made changes, they answered that with a resounding yes, which will have pleased him as much as the result, as much as the comeback, as much as Mac Allister’s stunning response.

“I was enjoying it [the Anfield crowd]. They [Atletico Madrid] are a very good team. Technically, in the middle, lovely players. It is not easy to press those players as they have quality. They have been playing together forever. We find another comeback after Nottingham Forest, after Newcastle. We still have this thing to improve in the beginning of the games, but I am happy as we have shown some character. This is the Champions League, you do not have easy games.”

"You can see he's football mad." ⚽Steven Gerrard on Andoni Iraola's passion and the impact he's making at Liverpool 👏🎙️ @laura_woodsy | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/M3qKhxt8HE

"It's difficult to ask for more." 👏Andoni Iraola reflects on Liverpool's winning start to their Champions League campaign.🎙️ @laura_woodsy | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vDH7bob0V8

Andoni Iraola has been speaking to TNT Sports and has confirmed that it was just cramp for the likes of Bradley Barcola, rather than an injury. Milos Kerkez also went off late with what appears to be just cramp.

So far, four of the five Premier League teams in the Champions League this season have played on this opening matchday and all four have won:

There is the final whistle at Anfield and Liverpool start their Champions League campaign with a 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid. Koumas is tripped by Le Normand and that should be it.

Liverpool think they have sealed it through Frimpong but the offside flag has gone up. First Munoz cuts onto his right and has a shot saved by Oblak. The ball falls to Frimpong, who slots home but he was clearly offside when Munoz took the initial shot.

Kerkez is currently down with cramp and his night is done. He will be replaced by Tsimikas and Liverpool will make their final change at the same time. Koumas comes on for Isak.

Atletico win a corner but it all stems from sloppy play in the centre of the pitch from Gravenberch. He has had a few sloppy moments since coming on.

The corner is flicked on by Hjulmand but ends up coming to nothing.

It isn’t the headline making performance, by any means, but that shouldn’t dilute the importance of Ronald Araujo’s contribution for Liverpool tonight and, indeed, against Ipswich last Friday. He’s doing what Liverpool wanted him to, providing versatility and leadership in their back four and - more than anything - quality. He hasn’t put a foot wrong.

Atletico win a corner out on the left in front of their travelling supporters. Grimaldo’s outswinger is flicked on by the head of Hancko at the near post but it goes over.

Isak has the chance to potentially seal the victory for Liverpool but Le Normand makes a crucial block. Le Normand has only just come on but already made a couple of defensive actions.

Liverpool win a corner out on the left with the last touch coming off Pubill, who was marking Van Dijk from a free-kick. Szoboszlai’s inswinger is headed away by Le Normand.

Digeo Simeone is making his final two substitutions of the night as Le Normand and Hjulmad replace Romero and Barrios,

Atletico bring on David, on loan from Juventus, for Baena.

Alvarez has a chance inside the Liverpool box but his shot is straight at Alisson. There are some appeals for handball but it hit Munoz from such close range that it is never a penalty.

Liverpool are making a substitution as Mac Allister, who scored the goal to put Liverpool in front, is replaced by Gravenberch. Mac Allister, who made some comments in the press conference yesterday about his sadness at not being offered a new contract, put in a good performance in the centre of Liverpool’s midfield. He was on a booking though so probably sensible to take him off when you can guarantee that the Atletico players would have tried to get him sent off.

We’ll see what happens in the coming weeks and months but there have been glimmers here with Florian Wirtz looking better than he has done with pace to pass to; if it clicks with him, Bradley Barcola & Alexander Isak it could be exciting but one game must be built on. It’s frustrating that Barcola’s night has ended with what appears to be cramp or tightness in his calf because he was getting more joy than he had done before half-time. The big challenge for Liverpool, too, is whether they have the nous to see this contest out.

The new Netherlands boss Xavi is in attendance at Anfield tonight, watching the likes of Van Dijk, Frimpong and Gravenberch, although the latter is still yet to come off the Liverpool bench.

This is a concern for Liverpool. Barcola has gone down and seems to have some pain in his left calf. Is it cramp or an injury? It will be a double change for the home side as Frimpong and Munoz come on. Barcola is given a standing ovation as he goes off and the Liverpool fans will be hoping it is just cramp. Ngumoha also heads off.

Diego Simeone is going to make his first two changes of the night. Grimaldo and Lookman come on

It is all Liverpool as they sense a third goal is there for the taking. Ngumoha does well down Liverpool’s left and pushes it past Pubill, who slides in and takes him down. Pubill is booked. He cannot believe it but I do not know why; a clear foul and yellow card.

That is a stunning strike from the Argentine. The ball falls to the midfielder just outside the box and he hits it first time. He hits the ball so crisply and there is nothing Oblak can do to stop it. Liverpool should have taken the lead through Barcola moments before they do now have the lead for the first time tonight.

Well, that’s one way to prove you might warrant a new contract. Diego Simeone most wonder how Atleti are losing a game they were controlling but Liverpool’s speed on the break is proving very good at causing chaos.

Barcola should have his first Liverpool goal and the hosts should be ahead but the Frenchman misses the target. Barcola drives forward, into the Atletico box, and you think he is going to slot it into the bottom corner but his effort goes just wide. Barcola could and perhaps should have a brace tonight.

The first half at Anfield is brought to an end and it is level at 1-1 at the break. Llorente gave Atletico the lead before Szoboszlai equalised for Liverpool. The home fans let the officials know what they think of their performance in that first half.

One added minute at the end of this first half.

There has been about five minutes of squabbling between the Liverpool and Atletico benches, so much so that Tommy Elphick - Andoni Iraola’s assistant - missed Dominik Szoboszlai score the equaliser. Tensions have only increased after a nasty little challenge from Cristian Romero on Alexander Isak. The half-time whistle might be coming at a good time to defuse the situation but you fancy the walk back to the dressing rooms will be spicy.

The conduct of the Atletico players is frankly embarrassing, not a massive surprise from a Diego Simeone side. Kang goes down clutching his face when there was barely any contact and then, unlike Isak, he does not have to spend a minute off the pitch.

Have your say in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

Moments after Liverpool equalised, Atletico have a decent opportunity to restore their lead but Baena drags his effort wide from the edge of the box.

Moments after Barcola could not take a big chance to equalise for Liverpool, Szoboslzai does. First, Barcola is denied by Oblak. Liverpool keep it alive inside the Atletico box and a simple sensational flick by Aruajo finds Szoboszlai, who finds the bottom corner with a clinical finish. Kerkez has been poor tonight but he deserves credit for his part in that goal as he was the player to initially win it back for Liverpool with a good press.

Liverpool look like a team that has been out of the Champions League for a couple of years and are only just finding its feet, which seems strange given they missed only one year in the last 10. They have glimmers of promise but they aren’t convincing anyone they will blow Atleti’s house down. One day everything will align for Atleti and they will reach another final. They have an outside chance this year, especially if Julian Alvarez - easily the best player on this pitch - has anything to do with it. Diego Simeone always has class strikers at the top of his team and Alvarez stands comparison with any who have gone before.

Wirtz has a great chance to equalise for Liverpool but his shot on the half volley is saved by Oblak. It would not have mattered anyway had the ball ended up in the net because Isak was offside before crossing for Wirtz.

Some of the officiating tonight has been appalling and the latest example is VAR taking a check on a possible red card for Mac Allister for a foul that is never a red card in a million years. The officials then take an age to give yet another obvious offside and, in the end, the referee gives it rather than the linesman. Atletico were renowned for years under Diego Simeone is being very tight at the back and in midfield, especially away from home. However, in recent years they have become more expansive and as a result are more open.

Liverpool win their first corner of the night at the Anfield Road End in front of the travelling Atletico fans. They take it short and Szoboslzai takes it towards the Atletico box. It appeared to be a very obvious foul on Szoboszlai right on the edge of the box but nothing is given. Barcola, who has won the Champions League with PSG in the last two seasons, is starting out on the right for Liverpool tonight with Ngumoha on the left.

Big test for Liverpool and it will be fascinating to see how this formation works out. It’s also a big test for Iraola against Diego Simeone, the wily and vastly experienced manager, who is immaculately dressed - as always - in his trademark black suit.

Liverpool have a chance inside the opening minute. Szoboszlai wins it inside his own half and drives forward. He then plays it out to his right to find Isak, whose shot from the right side of the box is dragged wide of the far post. A minute’s silence to remember the victims of the landslides in Nepal is impeccably observed.

The original “This is Anfield” sign has sold at auction for almost £150,000, 10 times more than its guide price.

The sign that hung above the players’ tunnel at Liverpool’s home stadium during the 1970s had been expected to fetch between £10,000 and £15,000 after being put up for auction on Tuesday and Wednesday.

But the “talismanic” piece of football memorabilia ended up being sold by auctioneer Budds for £149,500 to a UK private buyer.

The Argentine is into the final two years of his contract, which runs out in 2028. He arrived at Liverpool in the same summer as fellow midfielders Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai, who have both signed new contracts. Mac Allister was linked with a move away from Liverpool during the summer transfer window and was candid about his contractual situation in the press conference yesterday:

“I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract which, of course, makes me very, very sad. Everyone can see that I give my 100% for this football club every single day in training and games. Of course, I can have very good games [and] bad games, like everyone, but I always give my best.

“I see Dominik [Szoboszlai] and Ryan [Gravenberch] renewing their contracts and that makes me very happy because they deserve it. At the same time it makes me a little bit sad that I did not get mine. Of course, there is still time. The fans do not need to worry because I will give my 100% until the last day I am here. There were options to leave this summer. I think right now I am in the right club and I have the right mindset to give 100% for this club.”

Former Liverpool manager Rafa Benitez, who led the club to Champions League glory on that famous night in Istanbul in 2005, is in attendance tonight. Andoni Iraola has just shared a hug with his compatriot and perhaps Benitez will have a few words of advice for Iraola ahead of his Champions League debut as a manager.

The Dutchman has been in fine form at the start of the season for Liverpool, registering a goal and three assists in his first three games. He missed training yesterday and is not in Liverpool’s matchday squad tonight. Andoni Iraola has confirmed that Gakpo has a small adductor injury that he picked up in the Ipswich game last Friday but could be fit for the weekend against Fulham.

When Liverpool won their sixth European Cup in 2019, they lifted it in the Wanda Metropolitano against Tottenham. This season’s Champions League final is in that very stadium and Liverpool’s Champions League campaign starts tonight against the club that plays their home games in that stadium, Atletico Madrid.

“This is going to be a challenge, I hope, all the season because it would mean we continue in all the competitions. In this case, it is not the worst scenario because we played last Friday so we have had I think a good recovery. Probably it is going to be more difficult for next weekend, especially for the next game against Tottenham in the Carabao Cup because we will have just two days, game, two days, game. But we have to get used to this; it is what big clubs do. Definitely there is part of your mind where you have to think [about] the next games. But for us, the game tomorrow is very important.”

Ready for #UCL action 👊🔴 pic.twitter.com/XyOupLwsRe

Liverpool begin their Champions League campaign at home as they host Atletico Madrid at Anfield. These sides met at Anfield on matchday one last season, with Liverpool winning a dramatic game 3-2. Liverpool led 2-0 inside the opening 10 minutes before Atletico came back to level the game at 2-2. Virgil van Dijk then scored in added time to give Liverpool all three points before Atletico boss Diego Simeone was sent off for clashing with the Anfield crowd, resulting in a one-match ban.

Andoni Iraola earned his first win as Liverpool boss on Friday night as they won 2-0 away at Ipswich thanks to a quickfire early double from Alexander Isak. This will be Iraola’s first Champions League match as a manager.

“I think obviously it is a special night for me,” Iraola said. “Everyone talks [about] the Champions League nights at Anfield and also the first game is against a strong opposition, it is Atletico Madrid. [Diego] Simeone is doing an incredible job as a manager. To be all the years that he has been achieving every season the goals of the club I think is remarkable and definitely it is a big challenge for us. I think I played against him as a player, he was still a player, and I played against his teams when he was a coach and I also coached against him. So, we had a lot of precedent before. Definitely he has much more experience than me in this kind of games but I hope tomorrow we can give him a good game.

“It is one of the dreams, probably, when you start. It was difficult for me when I started my coaching career seven, eight years ago, to position myself in the position that I am right now, and I hope I can enjoy it. It is a big responsibility, massive challenge, but I feel privileged to be there in that dugout tomorrow [tonight] and now my thinking is about putting the team together in a position where we can play a good game, win the game and start strong in this Champions League.”

Atletico Madrid currently sit sixth in La Liga and suffered their first defeat on Saturday as they lost 3-0 at Athletic Bilbao. They did reach the semi-finals of the Champions League last season, where they fell to Arsenal 2-1 on aggregate.

“We are coming into a marvellous stadium and there will be a great atmosphere,” Simeone said. “We will have to look good from the start of the game because it will be full on. He [Andoni Iraola] works very well with the team, focusing on the tactical awareness of each player. It takes time to find the right path, but he is growing and improving and he has some very good players.”

Team news from Anfield to follow shortly.

#1864. Brighton injuries: Charalampos Kostoulas gives Stefanos Tzimas verdict after latest update

Charalampos Kostoulas is convinced Stefanos Tzimas has the mentality to come back stronger as Brighton's Greek connection prepares for a potential reunion on the pitch.

The two forwards arrived at the Amex in 2025, with Brighton investing a combined total of around £50m in the pair of young talents from Greece.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Tzimas signed from FC Nurnberg in January 2025 for a reported £20.8m, before joining up with the Seagulls that summer and Kostoulas followed from Olympiacos, signing in June for a reported £29.8m.

But their hopes of developing a partnership have been interrupted by injury. Tzimas suffered a serious ACL injury during Brighton's 4-3 defeat by Aston Villa last December, going down while pressing defender Pau Torres after 24 minutes.

The 20-year-old has been sidelined for almost a year. He made nine appearances for Brighton before the injury, scoring once and providing one assist.

Kostoulas - who has impressed this term with five goals and four assists - is delighted to see his compatriot make progress following his return to full training.

"I'm really happy for him," he told Sussex World. "It was a long time, but he was always really clear in his mind.

“He was looking at every day as one day closer to his comeback. He's really good. He has a really good mindset and I have big trust in him.

The pair have both featured in the same Brighton match, their competitive debuts in the 6-0 Carabao Cup win at Oxford United in August 2025.

However, they have yet to share the pitch: Tzimas was substituted in the 77th minute and Kostoulas came on a minute later.

Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler has been encouraged by Tzimas' return to first-team training, but is keen not to rush him back.

Speaking ahead of the 2-0 loss at Hull City, Hurzeler said: "He's a great personality, and that's also shown by his teammates. Everyone was happy for him.

“Everyone really appreciates that he fought that hard for this comeback.

"Now, of course, we have to be patient. It won't be that he will immediately be an option for us. He was out for a long time, so we need to give him time."

Tzimas was pictured in full training yesterday and there’s a slim chance he could be included in Thursday night’s Uefa Conference League matchday squad matchday squad to face Romanian league leaders Craiova at the Amex Stadium.

Keep an eye on the Sussex World website for further updates later today.

For Kostoulas, the prospect of finally playing alongside his fellow Greek in is an exciting one.

Asked what it would mean to have two Greek forwards representing Brighton, he added with a smile: "Also, two offensive players!"

#1863. Reports: Milan’s predicted XI to face Frosinone – Musah in midfield; Cisse benched

Ruben Amorim is expected to make one change to the starting eleven for Milan-Frosinone, according to the latest reports.

As the international break is over, Milan have used the last couple of days to prepare for Sunday’s clash against Frosinone. It’s a chance for the Rossoneri to make it three consecutive wins for the first time in the league this season, but as highlighted by Amorim, it’s a tough one.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The good news is that Mike Maignan is available despite the injury scare mid-week, while Strahinja Pavlovic has also been included in the squad. Amorim actually said that the Serbian wants to play, but it would be silly to rush him back.

#1862. ‘Really good’ - Brighton receive major injury boost as ex-Millwall ace set for Conference League debut

Femi Azeez is edging closer to his long-awaited Brighton debut after being spotted training with the Seagulls on Tuesday, ahead of Thursday’s Uefa Conference League meeting with Craiova at the Amex Stadium.

The 25-year-old winger is yet to appear for Albion since joining from Millwall last September on a four-year contract for around £15m.

Azeez arrived with a slight hamstring issue and also took a little time to adapt to Brighton’s demanding training programme.

Head coach Fabian Hurzeler previously stressed the need for patience, but offered an encouraging update last week. “He’s been training now for two, two-and-a-half weeks with the team,” he said. “He’s getting closer to his full potential. Now it’s about us not forcing things.”

Hurzeler praised Azeez’s pace and finishing, adding: “He is a really good finisher. He has really good speed.”

The Nigerian international was outstanding for Millwall last term with11 goals and eight assists, earning a place in the Championships Team of the Year. He can operate on either wing, giving Brighton another attacking option.

Brighton could also welcome back defender Pascal Struijk. The £18m summer arrival from Leeds has not featured since sustaining a thigh injury in the 2-0 win at Sunderland.

Hurzeler, speaking ahead of the 2-0 Premier League loss at Hull, said: “Femi Azeez and Pascal Struijk are back in training.

“Now we have to make a decision if they're an option for the weekend already or if we give them a little bit more time."

Brighton’s pre-Craiova press conference will be today at 2pm - check the Sussex World website for the latest team news.

A superb Kai Corbett strike early in the second half to put clear distance between the teams. Aveley were always chasing the game - and the Sports deserved their victory. Steve King's squad now sit third in the division, three points behind leaders Welling but with a game in hand.

They go across Sussex to Burgess Hill on Saturday.

#1860. I watched Rangers edge five-goal thriller vs Aberdeen and noted a title-winning trait and blossoming talent

Rangers produced a quickfire second-half comeback to beat Aberdeen 3-2 at Ibrox and move to within a point of Scottish Premiership leaders Celtic on Tuesday night.

After trailing to Brad Lyons' first-half header, which was deemed to have crossed the line by VAR despite Nico Raskin’s attempt to clear the ball, the hosts struck three times in a blistering spell after the interval through Ryan Naderi, Djeidi Gassama and Raskin.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Findlay Marshall's immediate reply ensured a tense finale, but Rangers held on to secure a vital three points and extend their unbeaten run to 14 matches. Derek McInnes’ side now have the chance to move top of the table on Saturday when they host high-flying Falkirk.

Lewis Anderson watched the action unfold for The Scotsman and picks out his three main takeaways from an absorbing five-goal thriller.

Once again, Rangers found a way to win. Their impressive run of results in recent months has been built on an increasingly familiar trait: an ability to secure three points even when performances fall short of the required standard. Against an enterprising Aberdeen outfit, however, McInnes' men were given a proper examination before eventually claiming another victory.

McInnes' decision to started with a back three, with Ben Godfrey drafted into the starting line-up for the first time since late July, raised eyebrows and ultimately failed to provide the defensive solidity he would have hoped for. The Dons repeatedly found opportunities to exploit the space around Rangers' exposed backline, particularly during a first half in which the visitors looked the more purposeful side.

Aberdeen played with an intensity that unsettled the hosts. Rangers’ combinations lacked precision, their wide players failed to make a sufficient impact and their build-up play was too laboured to trouble their opponents consistently.

McInnes’ response was decisive, with Kim Min-Su, Findlay Curtis and Tuur Rommens introduced at half-time. It signalled an acknowledgement that significant changes were required. Rangers emerged with greater urgency and attacking intent, and Naderi's equaliser provided the spark for a thrilling turnaround.

For a spell, Rangers looked capable of putting the contest beyond doubt, taking full advantage of the momentum generated by their early second-half goals. Yet just as they appeared to have wrestled the match under control, another defensive lapse allowed Aberdeen to threaten a comeback.

The victory was never entirely comfortable, nor was the performance perfect. But Rangers' capacity to respond to adversity and find a way remains an increasingly valuable asset. They continue to collect the points needed to maintain their title challenge and now have the opportunity to move to the top of the Premiership before Celtic take to the pitch this weekend.

Aberdeen will return north frustrated by the outcome, but newly-appointed head coach Mario Frick can take considerable encouragement from a performance which offered a glimpse of what his side might become under his stewardship.

For long periods, the visitors carried a genuine threat on the counter-attack and had sufficient opportunities to leave Ibrox with something to show for their efforts. Their defensive collapse during Rangers' devastating burst after half-time proved costly, with goalkeeper Marius Muller's handling error providing the catalyst for the hosts' revival.

Yet Aberdeen's response was equally striking. Having been left shell-shocked, they gathered themselves and went after Rangers with renewed conviction, refusing to accept that the contest had slipped beyond them. Findlay Marshall's goal, an impressive contribution from a player still only 20, gave them fresh belief and brought the prospect of an unlikely recovery tantalisingly close.

There was a vibrancy about this Aberdeen display which has been conspicuously absent for much of their recent past under Stephen Robinson. They played with ambition, conviction and a willingness to commit bodies forward, while their response to adversity suggested a resilience which Frick will be keen to nurture.

Aside from the damaging 12-minute spell in which Rangers scored three times, the visitors showed plenty of grounds for optimism. Their organisation was better, their pressing purposeful and their attacking play carried a level of intent which repeatedly troubled the hosts’ rear-guard.

The result will sting, not least because they had done enough in spells to believe a point was within their grasp. But there was little about this performance to suggest Frick intends to oversee a cautious rebuilding exercise. If anything, Aberdeen look set to embrace a more adventurous identity, which should please supporters.

Aberdeen have a seriously talented prospect on their hands in 20-year-old Findlay Marshall, who was influential throughout. The midfielder won the corner which led to Lyons' opener before scoring a sublime second-half goal after being picked out by Alexander Briedl, which set up a tense finale.

His energy and attacking intent made him one of Aberdeen's most dangerous players and offered Frick further evidence of the his undoubted potential. Marshall displayed a maturity and composure which belied his age, combining an impressive work rate with an eye for goal. In defeat, he emerged with considerable credit.

The Rangers No.1’s contribution was arguably as important as the three goals at the opposite end. His first-half fingertip save from Ayoub Mouloua prevented Aberdeen establishing a two-goal advantage. The Croatian’s work was not finished there. After the interval, he made a fine stop at his near post to thwart Nicky Devlin before denying Marshall as Aberdeen searched for an equaliser.

Rangers' second-half attacking burst will dominate the headlines, but without Pandur's crucial interventions the outcome could have been very different.

The Reds built on an encouraging win over Fleetwood Town on Saturday, which showed signs of an improved defensive structure, with a clean sheet to show for their efforts.

When asked about the significance of defensive reinforcements Ben Heneghan and Josh Flint, Blackwell said, “[They have been] massive, massive. We've got somebody who can win a header, which has been thrown on the shoulders of Priestley [Farquharson], but Ben's there and Flinty's not bad in the air.

Another player who had to adapt to fill a role for the team was Jonny Russell. With the Reds moving to a back five in the last two games, the Northern Irishman played as a wing back on Saturday and moved into the left side of the back against Barnet.

The former assistant to Neil Warnock said: “He's got a heart as big as a bucket, Jonny. He'll go through a brick wall for you.

“It was forced on us obviously to make that decision and pull [Charlie] Barker out and then take Flinty across, so we had to make a couple of changes because we'd lost Jude [Arthurs].

#1858. Rangers’ knack for winning ugly is becoming a habit but utility man wants fewer self-inflicted scares

James Penrice believes Rangers are acquiring the habit of winning ugly and grinding out results as their Premiership title challenge gathers momentum, but has warned they must address their tendency to surrender control after taking commanding positions in matches.

A gritty 3-2 victory over Aberdeen at Ibrox on Tuesday night brought Rangers to within a point of Celtic at the Premiership summit and extended their unbeaten sequence to 14 games. It was also another test of their resilience, with a disjointed first-half display giving way to an emphatic response after the interval, when Rangers struck three times in a blistering 12-minute spell.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The hosts had gone in at half-time trailing to Brad Lyons’ header, prompting McInnes to make a triple substitution and reshape his side. The changes had an immediate impact, with Ryan Naderi, Djeidi Gassama and Nico Raskin all finding the net during a devastating spell early in the second half. However, Findlay Marshall’s reply ensured Rangers were unable to enjoy a comfortable conclusion to the match.

Penrice, who operated in a midfield three alongside Raskin and Dan Neil, praised the character shown by his team-mates to secure another welcome three points, but was equally candid about the frailties which threatened to undermine the victory.

“Very mixed, I think,” he said when asked for his assessment of an absorbing contest. “We conceded in the first half, but came flying out of the traps after the break. I thought we were really good for 10 or 15 minutes. We scored the third and looked comfortable, but then we switched off. We made it difficult for ourselves again, but the main thing is that we walk away with three points.”

McInnes used the interval to make tactical changes, with Penrice crediting the substitutes for injecting the energy and intensity needed to wrestle control of the contest from Aberdeen.

“We made a couple of changes. I thought the boys that came on were brilliant, that real spark and energy,” he added. “We started the second half really well, but ultimately we need to score more. We could have done that and made it really easy for ourselves, but then again we switch off and we make it difficult.

“Ultimately, it's not a bad trait to be scoring late on sometimes and winning games, but as players we want to make it as easy as possible. Again, we’ve made it hard but we’re still winning games and going on a wee bit of a run now, so hopefully that continues.”

Penrice’s versatility has become an increasingly valuable asset for McInnes. Primarily a left-back, he has also been deployed in central and wide positions as the manager continues to adapt his tactical approach to suit each fixture.

“I'm not bothered where, I’ll play absolutely anywhere to help the team,” he admitted. “It’s a massive thing for me. We work on it [in training] but I've not really trained over the last couple of days, because I was feeling a wee strain so it was more just dealing with it. It's not alien to us, we've done it numerous times this season, guys playing in different positions.

“I've played in the middle, I've played out wide, so we should all be used to it now and we are. It just takes that adjustment period on the pitch but us as players we've got a responsibility when there's a plan in place and something's not going right we fix it ourselves. We don't need to go to the side and I think that's what the gaffer is looking for. He's looking for us to take responsibility on the pitch and we've got that now.”

Rangers have little time to dwell on their latest victory, with Falkirk due at Ibrox next on Saturday, a fixture that offers McInnes’ side the chance to leapfrog Celtic and move top of the Premiership table, having closed the gap on the leaders with their comeback win over Aberdeen.

“It's a massive incentive, but the league's not won in November,” Penrice declared. “It will be a difficult game. Falkirk are playing well and they've travelled well away from home. So we'll need to be on it. We can't go into the game on Saturday like we were tonight. We need to be better. We just need to concentrate on ourselves, it's another game to tick off, one at a time.”

#1856. Four first half goals for Hassocks in hammering of Hurst

Four first half goals away at Billingshurst showed Hassocks have not suffered any lasting damage from their midweek hammering in the Sussex Transport Senior Cup at the hands of Chichester City.

Chi relentlessly stuck six past the Robins on Tuesday night. Hassocks were equally unforgiving on Hurst, pocketing all three points before the half time whistle.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

No further goals were added nor needed after the break, allowing the Robins to take their foot of the pedal and James Westlake to rattle through the substitutions ahead of a huge upcoming five weeks which could be season-defining.

Hassocks go to Rusthall next Saturday for their first ever appearance in the third round of the FA Vase. A place in the last 32 of the national competition is up for grabs.

December then brings matches against Roffey, Guernsey, East Grinstead Town, Eastbourne United and Haywards Heath Town. Five games against teams in the top eight of the Southern Combination Premier Division all harbouring hopes of promotion.

"It's going to be busy, it's going to be hard," said James Westlake of those upcoming fixtures. "It is a tough run through until January time really. But those big games in the league are the ones we want to be competing in."

Billingshurst provided a different type of challenge. Several ingredients were there for a banana skin - a pitch already heavy before kick off, opposition fighting relegation and a popular former Robin in the home dugout.

Eddie French expressed his displeasure at the performance of the officials afterwards and it was hard not to have some sympathy for the ex-Hassocks favourite.

Certainly in relation to the bizarre series of decisions which saw the Robins awarded a penalty for their second goal of the afternoon, Nat Guest sent off and Billingshurst left to play for 70 minutes with 10 men.

Hassocks took the lead five minutes prior to that pivotal sequence of events. Playing down the hill, Omar Abdsami exchanged a one-two with Dan Perry to split open the centre of the Hurst defence.

Abdsami still needed to get around covering right back James Bendell. He did that via some quick feet before firing low and hard across Fraser Trigwell and into the far corner.

Trigwell provided another current link between the clubs whilst Hassocks introduced former Hurst midfielder Luke Brodie from their bench in the second half.

Then came the major talking point. Lewis Finney delivered a corner which Dan Turner met with a towering header. The ball was several feet over the line when it struck Guest in the hand.

Remarkably, the officials did not award the goal but instead gave the Robins a spot kick and sent Guest off for deliberate hand ball.

Chaos ensued with the surreal scenario of both Hassocks and Billingshurst players protesting against the same decision for different reasons.

Once order was restored, Finney put away the spot kick despite Trigwell diving the right way. And just to really rub salt into Hurst wounds, the initial corner Turner scored from was a clear goal kick too.

"I would certainly have been frustrated if that went against us with the awarding of the corner to start it all off," Westlake said afterwards.

"If you are a neutral watching the game, you would ask that the goal from Turner is given and it is not a sending off. It was a shame for them but I guess we already had a good foothold and would have been 2-0 up anyway."

Two very quickly became three and there was nothing controversial about the spectacular strike from Finney 120 seconds after his successful penalty.

Liam Hendy played a long ball forward which Perry won in the air. The flick dropped into the path of Finney, who hit a 25 yard dipping volley. Trigwell got a hand to it but could not keep it out.

Hassocks enjoyed near-total domination for the remainder of the first half with the Billingshurst X account posting at the interval: "To say this has been like the Alamo would be harsh on the Alamo as it has been more one-sided than that."

Tall striker Jamie Wilkes lent so far back that he was almost horizontal when putting a shot from a good position into orbit. Trigwell then made an excellent finger tip save diving low at his near post to keep out an Abdsami effort.

Having set up both Abdsami and Finney, Perry added the fourth himself five minutes before half time. Jack Troak started the move down the left and his square pass inside was beautifully back heeled to Finney by Darren Budd.

Finney glided past Jack Griffin and although Trigwell did well to parry away the shot, Perry followed up for a poacher's finish to open his Hassocks account.

Billingshurst will undoubtedly be happy to see the back of the Hitman. Five weeks ago he scored a hat-trick against them for East Grinstead Town with what turned out to be his final goals in a Wasps shirt.

French changed Hurst's shape for the second half and it allowed them to stem the flow of goals without ever really offering much going forward.

Ed Cooper did not have a serious save to make although Griffin and Kieran Britland both should have done better when shooting high and wide respectively.

Britland did at least have the excuse of losing his footing as he pulled the trigger. He was not the only one to slip and slide as the already challenging surface cut up massively the longer the game went on.

Chances at the other end for Hassocks came for Charlie Bonwick-Adams, who put a header straight at Trigwell. Finney guided a Troak cross wide of the front post and substitute Raging Joe Bull did everything right after overlapping Abdsami, receiving a pass and cutting inside only to shoot into an adjacent field.

Trigwell made an outstanding double save when pushing away a Budd piledriver from the edge of the box at full stretch before reacting quick enough to get up and deflect the follow up from Abdsami behind using his feet.

Turner hit a volley diverted behind by a fine block with the final opportunity of the game involving two more replacements. Lewis Croal headed down a cross for Big Alex Fair to shoot directly upwards rather than towards goal.

"We wanted to kick on in the second half but that obviously wasn't meant to be," Westlake added. "The lads have come off disappointed considering we couldn't score more goals. But a clean sheet, four goals and three points are the really important thing today."

Hassocks: Ed Cooper; Charlie Bonwick-Adams, Dan Turner, Liam Hendy, Jack Troak; Jamie Wilkes, Darren Budd; Devon Fender, Lewis Finney, Omar Abdsami, Dan Perry.

Subs: Liam Benson, Lewis Croal, Joe Bull, Luke Brodie, Alex Fair (used).

Starman: Lewis Finney converted a penalty for the second goal, scored a stunning volley for the third and set up Dan Perry for the fourth.

Baur was recently ruled out for up to 10 weeks with ankle ligament damage but manager Martin O’Neill had been waiting to see how the German international reacted once his protective boot was off.

Baur could miss the rest of the league stage though and O’Neill has acted before setting off for Portugal.

With Benjamin Nygren nursing a heel problem, O’Neill started with a midfield three of Callum McGregor, Luke McCowan and Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain on Saturday, while Oliver Sorensen is another option.

Meanwhile, O’Neill has challenged Celtic to complete their Europa League comeback after resurrecting hopes against Besiktas.

Celtic were heading for a fourth straight defeat and bottom spot when they went behind against the Turks but they were inspired by the introduction of Camilo Duran, Callum Osmand and Colby Donovan and sealed a 3-2 win.

They now face away games against Torreense and Omonia Nicosia as they bid to move up the table.

Looking back at their recent win, O’Neill told Celtic Player: “I thought it was terrific. Really terrific.

“Besiktas are a very fine football team. Very fine side. They were expecting to win and win handsomely. They’ve spent a lot of money. I think their wage bill is in excess of £100million. So from that aspect, it was a terrific win.

“The character of the side was really brilliant. Really, really brilliant to win so late, and to win in the fashion in which we did was terrific. So it gives us a little bit of a chance and we have to go and try to do something for these next two away games.

“If we make it through to the qualifying stages, it will be the first time any team has been beaten in their first three games and made it.

“So that in itself should be a target for us. The games are not easy, we know that. We need to win at least one of these two away games and we might even need four points to give us a chance in the last two matches.

“We have to take confidence from recent games and take that into the game on Thursday.”

Torreense sit 13th in the Portuguese second tier and will host Celtic 60 miles away from their home in Leiria, as their own stadium only has about 2,500 seats.

But they have already beaten Lillestrom and Ararat-Armenia in the Europa League and took the lead against Sunderland before the Premier League side netted a stoppage-time winner.

“They won the Portuguese Cup against Sporting Lisbon, which is some achievement,” O’Neill said. “I’ve been learning as much as I can about them and watching footage.”

#1852. GdS: Wins, consistency and goals for Ramos – the next steps Amorim wants Milan to take

Ruben Amorim wants to see more from his AC Milan side, starting this evening against Frosinone, and he believes they are capable.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) report, the aim for today’s match is to ensure the break didn’t disrupt the momentum, ashat happened following the September-October pause when Milan drew away to Sassuolo.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

This time, the opponent will be even tougher (at least based on league position), and Amorim knows it. For this reason, he has demanded the utmost focus from his players and has sought to fire up Gonçalo Ramos, who has only scored twice in the first 11 league matches so far.

The first issue the Portuguese forward needs to address is his finishing. In four matches – against Juventus, Lecce, Bologna, and Inter – he failed to register a single shot, while in two others (against Lazio and Genoa), he didn’t manage to hit the target.

That is simply not enough for a striker who cost €70m, plus bonuses and commissions. However, according to the former Manchester United manager, the fault does not lie with Gonçalo and instead is a team issue.

“Having another forward to assist Ramos and Camarda would certainly be an extra option, but our real problem is that we aren’t reaching the final 30 metres. We are among the worst teams in Serie A when it comes to shots taken and chances created,” he said in his press conference.

“As for Gonçalo, we aren’t putting him in a position to score. Cissé gets into the box with his runs, while Ramos relies on the team’s build-up play. In Genoa, both of our goals came thanks to him. We need to support him better through more possession and quick passing combinations in the final third.

“My goal is to win matches while helping the players perform at their best. We signed Ramos to score goals, but right now, he is helping me more than I am helping him.” A candid admission in defence of the striker he personally pushed to sign.

Compared to the win in Genoa two Sundays ago, Amorim is leaning toward not fielding four attacking players (Moreira, Cisse, Pulisic, and Ramos) from the start.

In yesterday’s training sessions, Cisse was left out of the starting line-up, which featured Musah and Modric in the middle, with Rabiot pushed further forward behind Gonçalo. Pavlovic has been called up and is eager to start, though he is not yet at 100% fitness.

“The choice of formation depends on the opponent and the team’s current state. I don’t believe that scoring more goals or winning more matches is necessarily linked to fielding more attacking players. Frosinone is an attractive side to watch, and speed is their primary weapon,” Amorim added.

“We rank second in Serie A for the number of sprints, and we have the tools to counter both their pace and their one-on-one ability on the flanks. We’ll need to be focused, as they commit more players to the final third than we do and are more clinical than us when winning the ball back.

“As for our season so far? I’m not satisfied with fourth place or all of our performances. We need to play better and achieve more in Europe, but we have grown as a team and in our overall attitude. We must keep moving in this direction.”

He concluded by sharing a Christmas wish regarding the transfer market: “January signings shouldn’t be based on the current league table, but rather on long-term planning. My Christmas wish is for us to win our next seven matches and get our injured players back. That is what I’d like.”

#1851. Charalampos Kostoulas identifies Brighton turning point under Fabian Hurzeler after James Milner trust

Brighton striker Charalampos Kostoulas believes earning the trust of his teammates has been just as important as his goals this season.

The 19-year-old has made an encouraging start to the 2026-27 campaign, with five goals and three assists in 14 appearances across all competitions as he establishes himself as an increasingly important figure in Fabian Hurzeler's side.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

It marks a significant step forward from his first season at the Amex Stadium, when he scored twice in 21 Premier League appearances, making just two starts.

Brighton head coach Hurzeler - who last season questioned Kostoulas’ commitment to training - is now impressed by the progress, particularly the forward's growing physical strength, work rate and understanding of the demands of English football.

But Kostoulas says there has been no dramatic change to his game. Instead, he has gradually learned what the team requires from him and become more comfortable in his role.

"Mainly, it's about understanding what the team wants," he said to Sussex World.

"For me, as a striker, with time and after some months, I started to understand that. With the minutes I've got and things like that, I gained the trust of my teammates and I want to keep going like that."

Hurzeler has previously highlighted the difference in the youngster's ability to compete physically, saying: "When you see him now and how resilient he is in personal duels, it's something completely different."

The Brighton boss has also praised his pressing and attitude towards improvement, describing a player who is becoming increasingly professional.

Kostoulas credits the manager's clarity and attention to detail, while revealing he has enjoyed the greater freedom given to him in the attacking role.

"He's clear with the instructions he gives on the pitch. He's always clear," he said.

"But I think I didn't change the way I was playing. Last season I could also do these types of things on the pitch, but I have more of a free role, especially in my position. I like it."

The transition from Olympiacos to Brighton was not without its challenges, however.

Kostoulas admits the biggest adjustment was the daily routine, with longer hours at the training ground, different training methods and a greater emphasis on meetings and preparation.

"The daily routine, I think, was the hardest," he told Sussex World. "We spend many hours at the training ground, more than I was used to in Greece.

"There are different types of training, a different approach to the game, more meetings and things like that."

He was helped by some of Brighton's more experienced players, with former midfielder James Milner playing a particularly important role during his first season.

"Most of the older players would come and say something to me as advice," Kostoulas explained. "Last season, James Milner was speaking a lot to me and trying to help me."

He still occasionally speaks to Milner, while Pascal Gross has also become an important figure in his development.

For Kostoulas, having someone to turn to is vital when moving to a different country and footballing culture.

"It's important to have someone to help you understand the way the team works here," he explained to Sussex World.

"It's totally different. If someone from here moves to Greece, they will also need time. It will be hard for them.

"You have to find someone you can trust, have a good relationship with, speak to and who can give you an understanding of most of the things here and what's expected."

There is also the prospect of sharing the pitch with fellow Greek forward Stefanos Tsitsimas, whose return from a lengthy spell out has delighted Kostoulas.

"I'm really happy for him," he said. "He has a really good mindset and I have big trust in him. I think he will do great."

Kostoulas was keen to avoid looking too far ahead when asked about Brighton's ambitions after their impressive start to the season.

Rather than focus on the possibility of challenging at the top of the table or making a deep run in Europe, he insists the squad are concentrating on the next match.

"We don't think about what will happen after six months when the season will be finished," he said to Sussex World.

"We're just enjoying every day, trying to be happy and win as many games as we can."

#1850. Who are Pluto Data Analytics? Celtic take leaf from Hearts in bid to enhance player recruitment

Celtic have taken a leaf from the Hearts model by taking the plunge into the world of data analytics.

The Scottish champions have announced a strategic partnership with Pluto Data Analytics in a bid to enhance their player recruitment.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The link-up with the London-based football analytics and predictive modelling company will initially run for three years, with scope for it to be extended.

Celtic’s recruitment strategy has been heavily criticised among supporters in recent seasons amid their struggles in Europe and increased domestic competition from Rangers and Hearts.

The club said that working with Pluto would allow them to “gain access to enhanced analytical tools and insights to support existing recruitment and football operations functions”.

The move comes two years after Premiership rivals Hearts partnered with Tony Bloom-linked Jamestown Analytics in a deal which helped elevate the Edinburgh club to a level where they were within minutes of winning the title last term.

Announcing their new partnership on Wednesday, Celtic said: “The objective is clear: to improve decision-making, identify emerging opportunities and support the club’s long-term football strategy.”

Hoops chief executive Michael Nicholson stated: “We are always looking for ways to strengthen our football operation and ensure that we continue to evolve in an increasingly competitive environment. We have been reviewing the options in this area in order to select the optimum model for our club.

“Our partnership with Pluto Data Analytics, an organisation with real quality and pedigree within this field, reflects our commitment to innovation and continuous improvement.

“Recruitment remains one of the most important areas of any football club. Our aim is to identify talent as effectively as possible, reduce uncertainty where we can and support our football staff with the best available information.

“We believe this partnership will strengthen our ability to support the Club’s ambitions both domestically and in European competition.”

Manager Martin O’Neill said: “While football is not an exact science, if the club can access and utilise new tools and new details, ultimately, we hope that such data will help us deliver the success we are all striving for.

“Our recruitment and wider football operations teams have already engaged with Pluto. Our plans in the short, medium and longer term are being developed and we are confident that our relationship will deliver real tangible benefit to the club over the next few years.”

Jon Godfrey, CEO of Pluto Data Analytics, said: “We believe that predictive data modelling combined with the allure and resources of such a famous institution will allow us to achieve great things in this partnership.

“Celtic has the capacity to compete at the highest levels of European football and it is an honour and a fantastic challenge to work relentlessly with the club on achieving the exciting goals we have put in place.”

Formed in 2020, the company has between 51 and 200 employees, according to its LinkedIn profile, with its office based at Tintagel House, Albert Embankment, London.

While Jamestown Analytics were well known in football circles when they arrived on the scene at Hearts due to their previous work with Brighton and Union Saint-Gilloise, much less is known about Pluto Data Analytics.

Under the 'What We Do' section on their company website, it states: "At Pluto, we combine sports intuition with the latest technology and big data sets to answer difficult questions across multiple sports. Our work goes beyond validating player performance: we help clubs find overlooked talent, assess tactical impact and make smarter decisions at every level of the game. From top-tier recruitment to identifying emerging stars in under-scouted leagues, we turn complexity into clarity through intelligent, fast and adaptable data tools."

Another section of their website, under Bespoke Recruitment, adds: "At Pluto, we use advanced machine learning to validate how a player might adapt in a new league. For example, how would a defender in Japan’s J1 League perform in the MLS in America? This kind of insight supports clubs to make smarter, more confident recruitment decisions across borders."

Celtic are currently the only football club publicly identified as a client of Pluto Data Analytics, although the company states on its website that its predictive models are used by "clubs around the globe".

Like Jamestown, Pluto also has a background in the betting market, with their website stating: "Our models have been battle-tested by clients in betting markets, validating our edge across multiple sports."

In another similarity, Pluto’s CEO, Jon Godfrey, is a former professional poker. Tony Bloom, who founded Jamestown Analytics, also played poker professionally although there is no record of the pair having crossed paths.
