#1849. Martin Odegaard bails out comically wasteful Arsenal

For much of this sticky night in Naples, Arsenal appeared to be starting the new Champions League campaign the same way they finished the last one: by erroneously smashing the ball into the stands behind the goal.

Memories of Gabriel Magalhães’s ballooned penalty in the final against Paris St-Germain remain fresh in the mind, and here his team-mates were lining up to produce their own versions. Bukayo Saka and Piero Hincapié, especially, delivered astonishing misses which were closer to entering orbit than the opposition net.

Thankfully for Arsenal, though, there was one player who was in no mood to relive the frustration of that shoot-out loss 14 weeks ago. Martin Odegaard has started this season in truly fabulous form and here he scored a truly fabulous late goal, fizzed into the corner from range, to cap another inventive individual performance and earn three points for his team.

Great play 😮‍💨Martin Ødegaard rounds off a wonderful passing move for Arsenal 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FrH6gW8Ak4

In five matches this season, Odegaard has already scored four goals. That is three more than he managed in the whole of last season. The Arsenal captain is fit again and he is flowing. As ever, when Odegaard flows, Arsenal flow.

“That’s what we need, the players with that mindset to decide the game and play with that personality,” said Mikel Arteta. “He has got that edge. He’s getting into those positions much more in recent games.”

In the end it was a thoroughly deserved victory for the Premier League side, who were superior to Napoli in every department. Were it not for their comically bad finishing, they would have guaranteed the result long before Odegaard’s 75th-minute strike.

Their expected goals figure suggested they should have scored more than four goals, compared to Napoli’s 0.22. In total, they registered 26 shots – the most of any Arsenal team on record in a single Champions League match, and the most on record a Napoli team has ever faced.

“With the amount of chances we generated, the scoreline has to reflect a very different result,” said Arteta. “The number of players that got into this situation, the amount of situations that we generated in various ways was something that pleased me a lot.”

There was, almost inevitably, another clean sheet for Arteta’s side. They had the best defence in the Champions League last season, conceding only seven goals in 15 matches, and they were largely untroubled here. Ezri Konsa was once again excellent, in only his second start for the club. He successfully wrapped up Rasmus Hojlund, the former Manchester United centre-forward, and was as calm in possession as the absent William Saliba would have been. A potential injury to right-back Ben White was a concern, though.

The Champions League is the one that Arsenal have never won and, you suspect, the one that Arteta really wants. Success in this competition would elevate Arsenal to a higher level as a club and fully establish Arteta as one of the great coaching minds of his generation.

To lose last season’s final in such painful circumstances clearly hurt the Arsenal manager, who was visibly distraught after that shoot-out defeat despite the obvious delight of winning the Premier League title. If you could give him the choice between retaining the league this season or leading Arsenal to their first European Cup, he would surely pick the latter.

Arsenal have now won THIRTEEN UCL League Phase games in a row 🔴🔥 pic.twitter.com/UmcfMYO13r

A trip to Naples in the first round of the league phase made for a lovely opening tie: atmospheric, intense and competitive. Napoli have had a difficult start to their campaign, losing two of three Serie A games so far, but they possess real quality and have a top manager in Massimiliano Allegri.

Even at the age of 35, the great Kevin De Bruyne still has power in his boots and schemes in his mind. When he tested Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya from range in the first half, it would have triggered horrible flashbacks in the minds of the travelling supporters. In his previous 17 starts against Arsenal for Manchester City, De Bruyne had scored eight goals and registered four assists. Thankfully for Arsenal, it was the only moment in which De Bruyne really threatened.

Throughout this game, Arsenal moved the ball around with precision and purpose. They created an extraordinary amount of chances, with Saka and Hincapié missing the best of them. Saka’s effort in the first half, when one-v-one with the goalkeeper, was strangely erratic. Hincapié’s opportunity, meanwhile, was laughable. Two yards out from goal, he somehow put the ball onto the running track that surrounds the pitch at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.

Despite all the wasted chances, Arsenal kept going. Odegaard, in particular, kept probing. His goal was gorgeous: a swift exchange of passes between him, White and Christos Tzolis resulted in the Arsenal captain firing his effort from the edge of the area. Delicate build-up, ferocious finish.

In keeping with the theme of the night, Arsenal should have scored more. Noni Madueke, for example, missed a one-v-one when it seemed like he had all the time in the world. But Odegaard’s intervention eventually proved to be enough, as he once again stood forward as Arsenal’s match-winner.

That’s all from us, but we’ll be back tomorrow night to bring you Man Utd’s return to the Champions League against Sabah!

"I think the chemistry, especially in the front players, has been exceptional." ✨Mikel Arteta tells @AnitaNnekaJones how impressed he's been by the connection between Martin Ødegaard and Christos Tzolis 🤝 pic.twitter.com/J6VOAMk4Lm

Arsenal extend their #UCL unbeaten streak 👏 pic.twitter.com/wFBga6lNrN

"We missed so many big chances"Mikel Arteta shares his thoughts after Arsenal's victory over Napoli 💭🎙️ @DannyJamieson | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/zT2bHcPoiH

Before all of that, Arsenal will now have to turn their attention to the Stadium of Light as they travel to Sunderland on Saturday.

They then face Ipswich Town in the EFL Cup on Tuesday night, before travelling to Brighton on the weekend.

Tue, November 24: Borussia Dortmund (H) 8pm

“Everything runs through Martin Odegaard,” said Cole on TNT Sports. “He can stand still and find space. He is at the peak of his powers and it is beautiful to watch.

“You can’t help but love watching him play his football.”

Plenty of praise for Martin Odegaard on TNT, with former Arsenal man Martin Keown heralding the captain’s behaviour.

“He’s setting an example to his players. He’s fitter, he’s hungry, and he did his talking on the pitch. He came good for his team.”

Couple that with his impressive chemistry with new arrival Christos Tzolis, and there is a lot of goal-scoring potential there this season. Three of the winger’s four assists have been for his captain, and we’re barely a month into the season.

The action has concluded around Europe tonight so here are your final scores from this week’s second night of European football:

Napoli did not register a shot on target in that second half, and it is clear how much Arsenal just dominated to keep the pressure on.

It could easily have been three or four goals for Arsenal had they had better finishing, but either way, they did not let their heads go down.

They kept pushing to see out the result and got the job done. Arteta will be very happy with that away result.

This has not been Arsenal’s most clinical performance but they got the job done.

Great play 😮‍💨Martin Ødegaard rounds off a wonderful passing move for Arsenal 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FrH6gW8Ak4

Napoli are fighting, but Arsenal hold fast.

Milinković-Savić waves his players downfield for the final minute but Olivera can’t control the ball well.

Napoli again, still trying to get their goal and De Bruyne gives them a chance with a through ball to David Neres, but the striker can’t get on the ball.

Ben White appeared to be in a little bit of discomfort a few minutes ago. He’s now been replaced by Martin Zubimendi for the final 10 minutes of this game. Declan Rice appears to have moved to right-back.

Martin Odegaard has played some outstanding football tonight (again) and that is an absolutely outstanding goal. The delicacy of the build-up and then the ferocity of the finish. Four goals in five games for Odegaard this season.

There will be alarm bells ringing for Allegri and Napoli, as they are heading for their third defeat on the trot. They have not created much of anything in this second half and you have to imagine that Arsenal will now make life very difficult for them.

The breakthrough comes and of course it is Odegaard! Finally they get their moment, hacing recycled the ball on the edge of the area.

Guimaraes to Saka before the winger sends the ball back to Odegaard on the edge of the box. He lifts a ball into the centre of the box where there are a lot of bodies, but Tzolis snatches at it and sends the ball into the rafters.

Christos Tzolis and Bruno Guimaraes getting ready to come on.

Politano and Alisson Santos make way for Antonio Vergara and Constantino Favasuli.

#1847. Eastbourne Borough warm hearts on cold night – as professional job sees off Aveley

Sometimes the arithmetic scarcely adds up. Saturday afternoon in the sunshine: for sharing eight goals in a lavish celebration of the sport, one point. Tuesday night in temperatures that froze the breath and numbed the fingers: for a routine 3-1 victory: three points.

But Borough's players, management and frozen supporters were not complaining. Steve King's side had played positively, stood up strong against physically powerful opponents, and they got all the unglamorous things right.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

A smart move for 1-0 on 24 minutes, and after an Aveley equaliser, a second goal on the stroke of half-time. And a superb Kai Corbett strike early in the second half to put clear distance between the teams.

Aveley were always chasing the game - and chase it they did - but the Sports deserved their victory, and King's squad now sit third in the division, three points behind leaders Welling but with a game in hand.

Credit, too, to the 529 hardy souls who wrapped themselves in layers of scarves, coats and headgear to enjoy a proper football contest in which the visitors also played their part. Team sport is for sharing - and just a little bit of shared suffering to cheer on your team.

King chose to shuffle the pack a little on for Aveley's visit. Liam Nash, Max Sheaf and Darren McQueen took a rest, and the manager bolstered his midfield with the return of Craig Eastmond. Paul McCallum took a lone striker role - although with ample support from the players around him. Aveley, robust and physically strong, lined up with a proper old-fashioned 4-4-2.

Early stages were quite cagey, but a goalmouth melee on 12 minutes saw Corbett's low effort cleared, and the momentum was with Borough.

Corbett, two-goal hero on Saturday, found Aveley doubling up on him: The Millers' staff had done their homework. And with the industrious visitors defending from the front, as the coaching jargon calls it, the Sports needed to turn possession into scoring chances.

But the patience and persistence finally brought reward on 24 minutes. Corbett's corner was met first by Elliott Johnson and then McCallum, but with Aveley throwing bodies on the line, both were blocked. But the second block fell invitingly for Freddie Carter, who blasted his shot high into the roof of the net.

Aveley had spent much of the first half-hour bravely covering, blocking, spoiling – but the 15 minutes before half-time saw the Essex side pushing forward and suddenly threatening to open up the Sports defence. On 40 minutes they swept through the inside-right channel and a lovely cross from Anthony Jeffery was met by big striker Matt Johnson for 1-1.

Borough's response was almost immediate: with the Priory Lane scoreboard glowing on 45 minutes, a sweet move into the final third was prompted by Matt Hayden, Eastbourne's gleeful young full-back, who found Terrell Egbri on the right. The bustling winger delivered a lovely cross, met by skipper Josh Rees with an unstoppable diving header to restore the lead.

The second half resumed as the first had left off - or almost. Aveley are a resilient, physical outfit - within the laws and spirit of the game - and they came at Borough with renewed impetus.

Question: would a single goal lead see the Sports survive a whole 45 minutes? Answer: Corbett. From a set-piece, the hero of Enfield slalomed through a ridiculously tight penalty area to deliver a rocket into the top left corner of the Mllers' net.

Aveley did have their chances - or at least the promising approach work. But they could not quite find that final piercing pass to open up the home defence, and Borough were disciplined, alert and resilient.

A night to freeze the breath. A match to warm Borough hearts. And with 22 victories in 24 games, King's men have the momentum, the belief, and that mental force-field to carry them into the deepest of Decembers and out the other side.

#1846. Celtic set for historic European first, why Torreense match is no banker and ex-Hearts man to watch

Celtic will encounter a European first when they take on Torreense in Portugal on Thursday night.

It will be the only time the Hoops have faced an opponent from the second tier of their domestic league in a Uefa competition as a result of Torreense claiming the first major trophy in the club's 109-year history last season.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Their shock 2-1 victory over Sporting Lisbon in the final of the Portuguese Cup in May to qualify for Europe for the first time in their history was the stuff of fairtytale. Think second tier Raith Rovers beating Celtic in the League Cup final in 1994.

Of course, by the time Raith came to play in the UEFA Cup the following season, they had gone on to earn promotion to the top flight. Not so Torreense. They lost lost 2-0 on aggregate to Casa Pia in the promotion/relegation play-off, meaning they remained in Liga Portugal 2 for the 2026/27 campaign.

They have since parted company with their cup-winning manager Luís Tralhão, who was sacked last month after overseeing a poor start to the domestic season, and replaced him with former Estrela da Amadora boss João Nuno.

Torreense currently occupy a lowly 13th spot in Liga Portugal 2 and will host Celtic in Leiria, 60 miles away from their home in Torres Vedras, as their own stadium only has 2,500 seats and does not meet Uefa requirements.

But park any thoughts of this fixture providing a banker win for Celtic. Torreense have already beaten Lillestrom and Ararat-Armenia in the Europa League and took the lead against Sunderland before the Premier League side netted a stoppage-time winner.

They sit 19th in the Europa League table, a lofty 13 places above Celtic, who belatedly put their first points on the board with a 3-2 win over Besiktas on November 5 after losing to Ferencváros, Benfica and Celta Vigo.

Nonetheless, this is a match Celtic should be looking to win if they are to retain realistic ambitions of becoming the first team to reach the knockout phase of the competition after losing their opening three league phase matches.

This is their most winnable tie on paper and failure to garner three points would leave Martin O'Neill's men with minimal margin for error in their remaining three fixtures - away to Omonoia, home to Marseille, then away to Union Saint-Gilloise.

Ten points, and a reasonably healthy goal difference is expected to be the benchmark for reaching the knockout play-off round. Nine points may be enough, but 11 points is the target to be absolutely sure.

Celtic should be looking at trips to Torreense and Omonoia, currently fifth in the Cypriot league, as an opportunity to reach nine points before facing the French and Belgian big-hitters in their final two matches.

A familiar face awaits them at the Dr. Magalhães Pessoa Stadium. Former Hearts striker Musa Drammeh has been with the Portuguese club since departing Tynecastle in the summer of 2025.

He was part of their cup-winning squad last season and has played 17 times this term, scoring two goals.

The 24-year-old Spaniard has history with Celtic, having made his SPFL debut against them in a 2-0 defeat at Parkhead in September 2024, and then scoring his first Hearts goal in a 4-1 loss at Tynecastle two months later.

#1843. Newhaven add to league momentum as Lancers are beaten

The Dockers looked the more confident team from the outset, taking the game to their visitors from the first whistle. Their positive start was rewarded when, with just six minutes on the clock, they took the lead.

The Lancing defence failed to deal with a Ross Barclay long throw, Billy Oliver held up the ball before laying it into the path of Lee Robinson, and Newhaven’s goalscorer extraordinaire did the rest; lashing the ball into the net with his left foot.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Lancing, though, responded quickly to the early setback and were level just five minutes later. A decent move culminated with Jay Popham finding space in the area, and he finished into the bottom corner to restore parity.

The early goalscoring wasn’t finished there. Before 20 minutes had been played, the Dockers were back in front. Matt Gunn rising highest in a crowed penalty to area to nod the ball into the net from inside the six-yard box.

Newhaven should have reached the interval further ahead. Tyler Capon headed an Ezra Roeg cross over after a flowing move down the left flank, before Capon again went close from a teasing Ash Wadhams cross. Seconds later, Robinson appeared to be bundled over in the area, only for the ref to write the challenge off as a coming together.

Robinson then had a chance to add to the scoreline, denied only by a last-ditch tackle just as he was about to pull the trigger.

The second half played out in a similar vein to the first, with Newhaven very much controlling proceedings.

Chances continued to come and go for the home side. Robinson sent a header wide after fine link-up play between him and Wadhams, before the striker was denied by a decent save from the Lancing keeper.

With 25 minutes to play, the game should have been dead and buried. As it was, the Dockers entered the last quarter somewhat fortunate to still be ahead.

Antoine Sharpe beat Ethan Pike to a long ball forward, but with the goal gaping he could only strike against the post from a tight angle.

It was a let-off for Newhaven, but one they soon capitalised on. With 14 minutes remaining, a moment of magic from Oliver wrapped up a much-deserved three-points for the Dockers.

Receiving the ball just outside the area, Oliver wriggled his way past numerous Lancing players, before keeping his composure and firing the ball into the roof of the net. A fine strike to cap another fine performance for the Dockers.

That victory makes if four wins in their last five games for Newhaven, and they will look to make it five wins from six when they visit Wick this weekend.

Ruben Amorim is not a coach who makes a habit of singling out individuals, but he made an exception in Saturday’s press conference.

As MilanNews recall, on the eve of the game against Frosinone, Amorim bluntly admitted that Christian Pulisic and Adrien Rabiot are the ‘irreplaceable’ players in the current squad. Their characteristics and their quality make them unique, in the eyes of the coach and many fans.

When the American and the Frenchman don’t play, the team’s fluidity and effectiveness suffer significantly. There is a stark contract between Milan when Rabiot and Pulisic play versus when both do not feature.

Amorim’s words were clear in his pre-match presser: “Every player appreciates having the club’s trust. And Pulisic’s new contract has helped. When he wasn’t playing, I told you he was still important for Milan, and we can’t forget about the injured players.

“And you understand how important he is. He doesn’t talk much, but he speaks a lot on the pitch with his play. He always wants the ball. He and Rabiot always lift the team up. I don’t like to talk about individuals, but I have to.

It’s worth noting that the coach emphasised the importance of Pulisic’s contract renewal too. This is also why the club are doing everything possible to reach an agreement for Rabiot.

“We want to create an environment where young players can see a realistic route from youth football through U18 and U23 football and ultimately into the First Team.

There had been a sense of optimism amongst United’s fanbase heading into the season after Michael Carrick picked up the pieces from Ruben Amorim’s turbulent reign to lead the club to a third-place finish last term.

Sunday’s result ensured United remain firmly in the drop zone after 11 matches, only one point better off than rock-bottom Crystal Palace with the worst defensive record of any team in Europe’s top five leagues.

If Pochettino was expecting to be supported with significant financial backing in his efforts to turn United’s fortunes around this winter, he will likely be disappointed.

After all, Reports this week suggest the 54-year-old will have a budget of ‘well under £50million’ to work with when the January transfer window opens for business.

Asked what Pochettino must address with his meagre funds while tackling United’s woes on The Dressing Room Podcast, Cole replied: ‘The spine. They haven’t got a striker, a worthy striker.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Midfield, I think they’re alright there for now because they’ve got Carlos Baleba and I think he’s a fantastic player by the way, they’ve got Kobbie Mainoo, Bruno Fernandes… I think they’re alright in that position.

‘I know the boy from Chelsea, Andrey Santos, he’s there, but I know he’s not tuned in yet because it’s high pressure right now and he’s a little bit off it. They’ve got Youri Tielemans as well. Then you’ve got the centre-backs…’

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

According to Cole, United missed a trick when they gave Chelsea a free run at signing Welbeck from Brighton in the summer.

‘I think it’s criminal they didn’t sign Welbeck,’ he added.

‘I think he’s wasted at Chelsea at the moment, they should have signed Welbeck. He’d have done alright!’

Eyebrows were raised when Pochettino named his team to face Liverpool on Sunday, with Matthijs de Ligt thrown in for his first Premier League start of the campaign.

There were signs of rustiness in De Ligt’s game from minute one and it was the Dutchman’s calamitous defending that led to Dominik Szoboszlai’s breakthrough – and Leny Yoro’s sending off – after only ten minutes.

‘I thought that was him [Pochettino] protesting already,’ Cole said of De Ligt’s surprise selection.

‘I think it was on the first or second day that he was in, he was already saying he wanted more control in the transfer market. I thought you negotiated that in your deal!

‘He’s chosen the right time to do it [make a protest], in a game like that.

‘This was a free hit for him and yes, he needs defenders. But I’ve said it before, INEOS have gone with signing forward first and then the next window they get a midfielder… who does that? So that’s what has happened.’

Cole went a step further on Pochettino’s decision to field De Ligt, adding: ‘I think it’s bang out of order, he’s been stitched up.

‘He’s obviously not fit, he can’t read it. When you’ve been out so long, you get your bearings wrong, you don’t know where you are on the pitch. It happens, right? So I give him grace for that.

‘The problem is that Yoro is not experienced. So if you’re going to bring in De Ligt, you’ve got to bring another experienced defender in with him.

‘If De Ligt is going to be there and Harry Maguire is there then it’s alright and if Maguire makes that mistake that Yoro made, I get it.

‘But Yoro is still young, he’s still learning the game. They’re both, to some extent, inexperienced at this moment in time so it’s the blind leading the blind.’

United will look to stop the rot when they switch their focus to Champions League matters away to Sporting on Wednesday evening.

Three days later, Pochettino’s men return to Premier League action at home to Brentford.

#1829. Barnsley FC defender Sam Gale takes accountability - now others must as autumn turns to winter

Many in his shoes wouldn’t have done. When you are in a survival fight, which Daniel Stendel's side plainly are - even though it is still November - fronting up and being brutally honest is at least a starting point.

Gale said there was a bit of that in the away dressing room at Valley Parade on an evening when Barnsley’s winless league streak extended to 11 matches.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Those at the top of the club must do the same this winter and take accountability if the beleaguered Oakwell outfit are to have any chance of getting out of the mess they are in and avoid playing fourth-tier football next season for the first time since 1978-79.

On the pitch at Valley Parade, it was a rinse-and-repeat performance from the Reds, who outperformed Bradford in attacking metrics, just as they did to Sheffield Wednesday on Friday. In both boxes, they remain wholly deficient and soft, even.

Reflecting on events on the night at Bradford, Gale didn't shy away from that damning word. Soft.

"I think if you watched that, I don't think you can dispute that”, the former Gillingham man told The Yorkshire Post.

"It hurts to admit (that), I'm a centre-half and pride myself on defending.

"Bradford were a team of men who defended their box and blocked and headed everything and made sure no-one had an opportunity and ultimately we gave up really poor goals.

"We're coming up to the Christmas period and games are coming thick and fast with plenty of points to play for. Seasons can be won and lost.

"You can really turn your season around or it can go the other way. We've got to be around each other, address what we have to and it probably means a lot of home truths with each other and we've probably got to all look at ourselves.

"There were some home truths in there at full-time (at Bradford). It was necessary and needed.

"Ultimately, the management team could do nothing to affect the goals. The goals were poor and had nothing to do with tactics, shape or formations.

"There were three long balls we didn't deal with. And we haven't put the finishing touch in their box. That's the difference.”

Gale was culpable for the first goal from ex-Reds striker Stephen Humphrys when he made a hash of coping with a goal-kick from Bantams keeper Jon McCracken. It was compounded by meek defending from Arley Kay, who was shrugged off too easily by the goalscorer.

How Gale, 22 - in his first season in League One - and Kay, who turns 19 in February, would benefit from having a hardened defensive lieutenant alongside them who knows the level to learn from.

Gale added: "It was poor from me for the first goal and it sets the tone.

"This was a perfect example of a game being won in both boxes.

"By a country mile, we were the best side between both boxes. But it's irrelevant, they defended their box and were savvy with blocks, pushes, nudges and not letting you have anything.

"In our box, they were also savvy with the same thing and they got opportunities from it. That was the story.

"After the Sheffield Wednesday game, we talked about set-pieces and how we needed to defend them better and we did that. We still conceded three poor goals which were very similar - probably a cut and paste of each other. It's not one simple solution unfortunately.

"All we can do is put ourselves first and come together as a team because it has to get better."

Between now and the close of play on January 1, Barnsley, who have taken a pitiful two points from the last available 33 - face several sides in the bottom half of the table, starting with AFC Wimbledon on Saturday.

Their points haul could well decide whether they have a realistic chance of survival before addressing things in a January window they simply cannot afford to get wrong.

In the circumstances, Barnsley's support was admirable and stoic at Valley Parade. Their patience did snap at the end when a late penalty from Jake Beesley made it 3-0, but it was understandable.

"They are within their rights to be unhappy. Barnsley is a big football club with a big history and we're bottom of League One," Gale said.

"I'd be negative too if I was a fan - I'm a football fan myself - and paying my hard-earned money and travelling up and down the country to watch my team not win in 11 games, I'd have something to say as well.

"We've just got to take it and wear it. They are the reasons we are playing for this football club. Going into Saturday, we've got to block out the noise and give them something to cheer about."

Michael Carrick’s successor is said to be keen on adding a striker to his ranks to cover for the injured Benjamin Sesko, but tightening up his backline will also represent a priority.

#1824. Braver and stronger – Mansell lays down challenge as Burgess Hill Town seek league turn-around

So says boss Gary Mansell after the Hillians let a 2-1 lead slip at Stanway Rovers on Saturday to make it three points from the past 18 available.

Harry Lawson and MoM George Vorster put Hill 1-0 and 2-1 up in Essex but despite the second coming with only 15 minutes left, Mansell’s men conceded with eight to go.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

They should be lifted for the league campaign by Tuesday night’s 6-1 Velocity Trophy win at Crowborough, with Jack Strange, Yoan Edoukou, George Vorster (2) and Shamir Fenelon (2) scoring.

Mansell was asked after the Stanway draw how he felt and said: “The same as after the last few games with this little run that we’re in.

"We just can’t get over the line. We can’t fault the boys’ effort and work-rate, which was superb. In the second half we were on the front foot again.

"But we’re a little nervous going the other way at times – particularly when we’re in front. And ultimately, that mindset is not helping us.

"When we go 2-1 up we stop doing what we were doing. People think the right thing to do is to drop deep and tighten up. But all you do is invite pressure into areas where you then give away a cheap free-kick and you get punished.

"We need to be mentally stronger and control a game better by staying brave in possession and keeping the ball, which doesn’t allow them to have the ball. It’s all about playing the game in their half rather than our half.”

Mansell does not think Hill were a long way off becoming a winning team again.

"We’re struggling to get over the line because of nervousness around the group. This is a situation we haven’t been in for the three years I’ve been at the club,” he added.

"All the games have been tight other than the Enfield game. I don’t think we’re a million miles away. We’re drawing games that could go either way. We just need to get one over the line to kick-start something.”

Mansell thanked fans for continuing to turn up in good numbers. “It was a good turnout (at Stanway) considering how far we were from home. We do appreciate the support away from home.

"Stick with us, we’ll turn it round and get some wins and we will be smiling again.”

They host in-form Eastbourne Borough on Saturday.

Mansell said: “We’re not going to shy away from anything. We’ll keep plugging away trying to win games. We’ll go into Saturday as positive as we can.”

#1822. How Sheffield United's 'dinosaur' changed tactics to turn game against Southampton

A game which began like a demonstration of how short the Blades were of the Championship elite ended with them proving they have what it takes to mix it with them.

For half an hour the Blades were outclassed by a Saints side who looked Premier League-ready. The Blades had only just over 20 per cent of the ball, which for them in a Championship home game is extremely rare.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

When Hamza Choudhury gave it away and failed to stop Lewis Dobbin curling the ball in, it was no less than the Saints deserved.

But from that unpromising start, the hosts turned it around. The second half was pretty much all them, so when Daniel Peretz saved brilliantly from Tahith Chong in the 83rd minute, you wondered if it was going to be one of those nights.

But the drama was just beginning. Jordan Ayew, who had shown what mood he was in with a nutmeg in the middle of the pitch, produced another in the 90th minute as he beat two men along the byline and teed up Sydie Peck to equalise. It still could have all been for nothing had Blades goalkeeper Michael Cooper not made a crucial save one-on-one with Samuel Edozie in the third added minute.

“The concentration of Michael was absolutely outstanding and the save was great,” commented Wilder.

“It would have been incredibly cruel if we'd have not got a result.

"There would (still) have been a certain amount of pride - not enjoyment because when you play as well as that, you have to get something.

"But I think I'd have put my head on the pillow and I would have gone, whatever the result, I don't think they've been dealt with like we've dealt with them in the second half."

As for the other bit, Tonda Eckert played the Blades the compliment of moving the player who normally operates in the hole in front of James Ward-Prowse and Flynn Downes to sit between them and the back four.

"They've got really technical players, and we didn't get to grips with their shape," admitted Wilder. "They had control of the game, they had seven touches in our box in the first half.

"So the old man, the dinosaur, had to get to grips with their press, our press, which we did after half an hour.

"We just wanted the two wide players to jump a little bit earlier and we needed to get around their six (holding midfielder) because the six was dominating and dictating the game. So we stuck somebody a little bit higher, got around their six and had a little bit of a change at the back, just slid over and got more pressure on the ball. In the second half we've had 31 touches in the box, 16 shots, 71 per cent possession.

"We made really good footballers resort to just clearing the lines for the last 20, 25 minutes. Sometimes, when you look back on draws, it's bigger than just the draw, with the performance against a side of the quality that we played against."

#1820. CM: Adidas want to launch €500m Milan era with a big-name signing – the candidates

AC Milan and Adidas will be back together again from 2028, and the German brand want to launch the new era with a bi bang.

As Calciomercato.com write, Milan will return to being an Adidas club again, as they have been for three previous spells. The two brands became so closely linked above all by the successes of the 2000s under Carlo Ancelotti, before PUMA took over in 2018.

The contract with Adidas – which will begin in the summer of 2028 – is quite a sensational deal for the industry and for the club’s final years in terms of sporting results. It will bring in €50m per season for 10 seasons, the highest in Serie A by some margin.

Ten years ago, the Rossoneri signed a €14m per season contract with PUMA, which was renewed in 2022 to reach around €25m per season.

Adidas have already invested heavily in Milan and they want to strengthen the ‘alliance’ further. A lot depends on building a squad capable of playing a leading role in both Serie A and the Champions League.

For this reason, Adidas are hoping to help Milan land a world-class player. Napoli midfielder Scott McTominay could gain momentum in the coming months as an idea, as the former Manchester United player is one of Adidas’s most important players worldwide.

Bruno Fernandes is another name to keep an eye on. The Manchester United captain left Italy many years ago as a promising youngster and now wants to return as a top player. The Portuguese is a possible candidate, even if he is currently twinned with Nike.

Last but not least – in terms of consideration and feasibility – is Real Madrid’s Endrick. Milan are ready to make him one of the symbols of their new project and have a bid of €60m plus bonuses ready to try to break down Los Blancos’ wall.

Jose Mourinho is the main obstacle between the Rossoneri and the Brazilian star, but Cardinale is unwavering and ready to do everything possible to bring him to Milanello as early as January. The money from Adidas could help land Endrick, who is with New Balance at present.

#1818. Palmer and Rogers complete 12-minute rescue mission to save Chelsea

Xabi Alonso needed the cavalry – and referee Jarred Gillett – to stop Chelsea making a quick exit from the Carabao Cup and, boy, did they come up trumps for him.

Chelsea had looked to be heading out of the competition shortly after half-time, but, in Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, Alonso has a cheat code that is capable of masking even the worst defending.

Alonso’s side have shared 26 goals in the five games they have played this season. It has certainly been an entertaining start by Chelsea’s latest manager.

Palmer, Rogers and Pedro Neto stepped off the substitutes’ bench to complete a stunning rescue mission against Leeds United. Palmer scored twice, Neto once and Rogers helped himself to at least a hat-trick of assists. He claimed it was four, but the record books may say three.

When it was announced Palmer had been awarded the player of the match, Rogers responded by saying: “Mate, I got four assists. I can’t believe that! That’s mental. He scored a pen!”

"Mate, I got four assists!" "That is criminal!" Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer arguing over the POTM award! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/X2PkPnSGDk

Chelsea had looked down and out, when, just three minutes after Alonso’s quadruple half-time change, Leeds doubled their lead. But four goals in an incredible 12-minute spell turned the tie on its head and it was Alonso’s substitutes who Chelsea had to thank.

Palmer, with some help from Gillett, was the first to come to the home side’s rescue. Four minutes after Brenden Aaronson had put Leeds 2-0 up, Gillett pointed to the penalty spot after Daniel James had stood on the foot of Pep Chavarría.

It looked like a harsh decision on Leeds and proved to be almost as big of a game-changer as Alonso’s substitutions. Palmer stepped up to score the resulting penalty.

Cole Palmer pulls one back for Chelsea from the spot! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/BUv6h1wTPQ

“Nobody in the stadium, not one player was asking for a penalty and he gave the penalty,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, said. “All of a sudden their players came into the game. The momentum was on their side. Situations can change the whole momentum of the game.”

Stamford Bridge sensed a comeback and in the 55th minute, Rogers nudged the ball into the path of Palmer who produced a brilliant curling finish to beat Michael Zetterer, the Leeds goalkeeper.

TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6

Reece James then went close, before Neto completed the turnaround on the hour mark. Palmer found Rogers, who in turn picked out Neto and he sent Stamford Bridge wild by sending his shot into the corner of the net.

"This is a comeback of comebacks!" Pedro Neto scores and Chelsea have turned it around eleven minutes after going 2-0 down! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/FTPuWcFqEX

As Farke waited to make a quadruple substitution of his own, Danny Welbeck got in on the act by collecting the ball from Rogers, spinning and scoring.

Class from Danny Welbeck 😤 pic.twitter.com/FUFKxlzXDz

That should have been that and the atmosphere could not have been more different from half-time, when Chelsea fans had booed off their side after watching them fall a goal behind.

Reggie Watson, Chelsea’s 16-year-old debutant, Malo Gusto, Estêvão Willian and Jamie Gittens were hooked at half-time by Alonso, who said: “For sure, I take responsibility for all of them. No player to blame. It’s the decisions that we took.

“I know that probably I haven’t taken the right decisions for them to show their best level. It’s something that I will analyse and learn from. So it’s my responsibility and we had to make decisions at half-time. And we have seen another second half with another quality.”

Goalkeeper Mike Penders was one of the nine changes made by Alonso. He produced a superb double-save to first keep out Aaronson and then recover to tip Tarik Muharemovic’s header out from the corner.

Conor Coady was impressed with that Mike Penders double save in the first half 👏 pic.twitter.com/6NJqFDvnzk

But the Belgian flapped at the corner, which gave Harry Wilson a second chance to get his delivery right. And he did just that by finding Muharemovic at the back post to head the ball into the net.

Valentín Barco survived Alonso’s changes, but was partly at fault for Leeds’s second goal just after the break. He lost the ball and Ethan Ampadu galloped away from Rogers before crossing. Lukas Nmecha got the slightest of touches and Aaronsen smashed the ball into the net.

"Chelsea cut apart AGAIN !" Brenden Aaronson makes it 2-0 to Leeds 🔥 pic.twitter.com/LlJNpqXHav

The substitutes then took over, as Chelsea shocked the visitors before Leeds substitute Dominic Calvert-Lewin gave his team hope by reducing the deficit with 15 minutes remaining.

Any thoughts of a Leeds comeback were quickly erased, however, as Barco netted his first Chelsea goal from a Rogers pass, which may have taken a slight touch to deny him a fourth assist in the record books. Welbeck added a sixth in time added on.

Valentín Barco gets Chelsea a FIFTH! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/XnhgvhBpL9

On the defeat by Chelsea, Farke said: “The referee had the idea to give a penalty. No one in the stadium was asking for it, no one of their players was asking for it, but he spotted a situation where he thought he would give a penalty.

“All of a sudden they scored the goal, then their players came into the game at half-time, the whole stadium after being relatively quiet for 60 minutes they of course were there then. The momentum was all of a sudden on their side. In football small situations can change the whole momentum of a game and this happened.”

"100% I meant it!" 😅Morgan Rogers says he is really enjoying his football after he helped Chelsea beat Leeds 6-3 in the Carabao Cup! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/7uUQb6eIla

Here’s a reminder of the assist in question. Did Rogers mean it? Let us know in the comments beneath this live blog...

TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6

"Mate, I got four assists!" "That is criminal!" Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer arguing over the POTM award! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/X2PkPnSGDk

On the message from the manager at half-time, Palmer told Sky Sports: “Just up the intensity, play a bit more, become more alive because I think the first half was flat, everyone agreed in the changing room, so we stepped up.

Asked whether Alonso’s message was delivered calmly, he said: “At the start, but then he got a bit angry. But it was alright.”

On Chelsea’s half-time changes, Conor Coady said on Sky Sports: “I think the credit goes down to [Alonso]. He made a bit of a statement by doing that at half-time. Four subs is a lot to do at half-time but it was needed. Listen, we said about the first half that it was kind of like the players hadn’t played with each other, and then the big guns came on... They were electric at times.”

A crazy match which was decided by Chelsea’s superb substitutes. Alonso took action at half-time and was rewarded with six goals in a madcap second half. Palmer hauled Chelsea back into the game, Rogers collected a handful of assists and Neto scored the go-ahead goal. You wonder what this match will do for the likes of Estevao and Gittens, though.

Chelsea 6 Leeds United 3 (Welbeck) Pure reflexes from Welbeck, who diverts Barco’s wild effort beyond Zetterer.

Palmer has the hat-trick ball on his mind and attempts an audacious chip but just gets his angles wrong. Any guesses who laid on the chance? Rogers. Of course.

Fans in the away end have resolved they have seen enough and are now heading towards the exits. Stach attempts to launch a counter but his raking cross-field ball is far too heavy.

Rogers drifts out to the left and wins Chelsea a valuable corner. James walks over to take it to rapturous applause from supporters there.

Leeds look to break but Wilson mistimes his run and is caught offside.

There will be six minutes of time added on.

Chance! Okafor darts inside of Neto and spins in a teasing ball to the back post but neither Calvert-Lewin nor Tanaka are able to reach it.

Shouts for a Leeds penalty fail to pique the interest of referee Gillett. Gudmundsson was felled on the left of the box but the contact looked minimal.

A tap on Barco’s head from Wilson provokes some histrionics from the Argentine but Jarred Gillett calms all parties down.

Leeds are still pushing. Stach’s effort from eight yards out is closed down before Tanaka’s strike from the edge of the box is smothered by James.

Alonso goes into the book, apparently for straying too far outside of his technical area.

Chelsea 5 Leeds United 3 (Barco) Rogers lays on his fourth assist of the match, driving towards the byline before flashing a searching ball across the face of goal which Barco spears past Zetterer at the far post. That should be that, right?

Valentín Barco gets Chelsea a FIFTH! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/XnhgvhBpL9

Gudmundsson replaces debutant Bard down Leeds’ left.

Chelsea 4 Leeds United 3 (Calvert-Lewin) Game back on? Okafor is afforded far too much space down the left by a tiring Chelsea back line and his cross finds Calvert-Lewin who plants the ball past Penders to reduce the deficit to just one goal. What a tie this has turned into!

Leeds win a corner, which falls to Stach on the edge of the box but his effort is charged down.

It will be a source of acute anguish for Farke that Chelsea’s fourth goal came before he could make his four changes: Stach, Calvert-Lewin, Tanaka and Okafor eventually replace James, Nmecha, Longstaff and Aaronson. Conversely, it should be to Alonso’s credit that he took action early - his substitutes have decided this tie.

Chelsea 4 Leeds United 2 (Welbeck) Rogers gallops on to a simple ball down the right channel and his cutback (towards Palmer) is picked up by Welbeck who spins before firing beyond Zetterer, leaving three Leeds defenders sprawled in front of him. He cares not, and absorbs the love of the crowd in the near corner.

Class from Danny Welbeck 😤 pic.twitter.com/FUFKxlzXDz

Palmer goes close after having found a yard of space on the edge of the box. His strike spears through a thicket of limbs in Leeds’ box but Zetterer pulls off a strong save to deny the Englishman a quickfire hat-trick.

Chelsea 3 Leeds United 2 (Neto) Just 11 minutes after going 2-0 down, Chelsea find themselves ahead. Palmer threads a through-ball through the middle for Rogers, who slides in front of his marker to an open Neto who sweeps the ball beyond Zetterer. Leeds punished for leaving themselves two vs two at the back there.

"This is a comeback of comebacks!" Pedro Neto scores and Chelsea have turned it around eleven minutes after going 2-0 down! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/FTPuWcFqEX

Chelsea have got their tails up and Palmer almost lays on a go-ahead goal but James cannot turn in his cross from the left.

Chelsea 2 Leeds United 2 (Palmer) Wow! Palmer has turned this game on its head. And it’s so, so simple. Acheampong’s throw-in is knocked down by Rogers into the path of Palmer who works in from the right, passing the ball around a Leeds defender and past a rooted Zetterer.

TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6

Chelsea 1 Leeds United 2 (Palmer) Palmer makes no mistake. He goes right, and while Zetterer guesses the right way he cannot get there and Chelsea are back in business.

Cole Palmer pulls one back for Chelsea from the spot! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/BUv6h1wTPQ

Chavarria is caught by James in the box and the referee points to the spot. That came from nowhere.

Chelsea 0 Leeds United 2 (Aaronson) Amapadu deserves so much credit here. He steals the ball from Barco high, bursts beyond Rogers on the right and while Nmecha cannot turn in his cutback, Aaronson arrives late to stroke the ball past Penders and double Leeds’ lead.

"Chelsea cut apart AGAIN !" Brenden Aaronson makes it 2-0 to Leeds 🔥 pic.twitter.com/LlJNpqXHav

Alonso resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes at the interval. Palmer, Rogers, James and Neto enter the fray in place of Estevao, Watson, Gittens and Gusto.

Big cheers from the Chelsea fans at half-time, as Cole Palmer, Pedro Neto, Morgan Rogers and Reece James have all come on to warm up and are stripped off ready to play. Alonso is sending on the cavalry.

The delayed kick-off has knocked us out of kilter with tonight’s Champions League matches, but here are the live scores:

Liverpool 2 Atletico Madrid 1Paris St-Germain 4 Slovan 0Napoli 0 Arsenal 0Sporting CP 1 Galatasaray 1

Boos at half-time from the Chelsea fans. Their team were pretty awful, but booing so early in the season. Really?

There is only one minute of time added on and Watson earns himself a booking for a late challenge on Wilson before the half-time whistle is blown. It will be interesting to see how long Alonso waits before turning to his bench.

Justin, James and Wilson have got a lot of joy down Leeds’ right, rotating in Chavarria’s orbit. It has been difficult for Chelsea to pin them down and Gittens’ attacking threat has been blunted as he attempts to track their movements.

Better from Chelsea. Watson does well to regain possession high and Estevao takes over, darting towards the by-line. His cutback is directed towards Welbeck but he is beaten to the ball by a Leeds toe and it is played behind for a corner which comes to nothing.

Chelsea are really struggling to build up a head of steam, with individual mistakes proving costly.

Gittens and Estevao both end up on the left and the former works infield before firing a shot at Zetterer which the German parries behind for a corner. Perhaps Chelsea’s most dangerous moment of the half.

The corner is played short with the ball eventually falling to Barco on the edge of the box but his mis-hit effort trickles wide.

Gittens rescues an overhit Acheampong cross and finds Barco on the edge of the box, but the Argentine’s effort is charged down. Leeds spring a counter and their sweeping move up field earns them a corner.

Wilson floats another delivery to the back post to Muharemovic, but he cannot replicate his earlier goal.

Farke will be delighted with what he has seen so far. It is all well and good Chelsea allowing Leeds the ball, but they have to break incisively when openings arise, and they have not done that.

Big chance for Leeds! James bursts down the right and the Welsh winger dinks in a cross to the far post which Justin cannot get past Acheampong, but while Longstaff is first to the second ball, he can only sky the shot over the bar.

Leeds’ goal has stirred something inside them and they look motivated to score a second. Ampadu launches a long throw from the left which ricochets off a couple of players before rolling out for a Chelsea goal-kick.

Chelsea 0 Leeds United 1 (Muharemovic) Set-pieces have been a massive feature of Leeds’ game this season and here they take the lead with the simplest of corner routines. Wilson floats the ball to the back post where Muharemovic is waiting, unmarked, and he loops a header over Penders into the net. Such a shame for the Chelsea keeper as he had just pulled off a stunning double-save.

"The set-piece routine does it again!" Tarik Muharemović puts Leeds in front against Chelsea! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/UxeJ3xgL56

Barco slips on the far side and in doing so concedes a corner rather comically, to the delight of the travelling supporters. The delivery is met by Lacroix and Leeds are unable to create anything from the second phase of the set-piece.

There is an intriguing duel developing down Chelsea’s right as Bard looks to contain Estevao. The French wing-back has done a decent job so far.

Estevao attempts to free himself of Bard’s clutches and drifts inside, Chavarria then almost picks him out with a cross from the left but Leeds just about clear their lines.

Justin plays in a cultured through-ball from a wide-right position to James but Chavarria does well to snuff it out. Leeds are making the pitch as big as possible and spaces are beginning to open up as they did at Fulham on the opening weekend.

Although Penders’ shot-stopping has not yet been tested, he has shown some nifty footwork, sweeping up any loose balls that make it past Chelsea’s back three/five.

Big chance! Chelsea spring a surprise attack as Chavarria sets Gittens away down the left. He works the ball infield to Welbeck who lays on a great chance for Estevao but Justin darts back to take the ball off the Brazilian’s toes. A brilliant piece of last-ditch defending.

Gittens gets a shot away, a tame effort straight at Zetterer from 22 yards out as he cuts in from the left. The correct intent, though.

Leeds look to circulate the ball across their back line. As mentioned pre-match, Chelsea will not mind letting their opponents get on the ball as they set out-of-possession traps. Aaronson eventually dribbles off the pitch on the far side.

Chelsea’s Argentine midfielder, Valentin Barco, is being booed by the Leeds fans every time he touches the ball. Barco will already be used to getting that treatment, as it has even happened to him while he’s been a substitute this season.

In other news, there’s a real Borussia Dortmund vibe to this Leeds away kit.

Leeds supporters boo Argentina World Cup squad member Barco’s every touch, and another Leeds foul, this time Justin on Gittens, prompts a second Chelsea free-kick.

A couple of early touches for Watson who plays a neat pass around the corner. Ampadu then lands a late tackle on Lacroix and Chelsea earn a free-kick in their own half.

Although there are still some empty seats, we are finally under way. Chelsea in their customary all blue, kicking from right to left. Leeds in their yellow away strip.

Chelsea and Leeds emerge from the tunnel, led out by Colwill and former Chelsea defender Ampadu. Here’s a reminder of the teams in full:

Chelsea Penders; Gusto, Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill, Chavarria; Watson, Barco; Estevao, Gittens; Welbeck

Substitutes Martinez, Hato, Fofana, James, Neto, Palmer, Quenda, Rogers, Pedro

Leeds United Zetterer; Justin, Bijol, Muharemovic; James, Ampadu, Longstaff, Bard; Wilson, Aaronson; Nmecha

Substitutes Trafford, Gudmundsson, Elvedi, Bogle, Tanaka, Stach, Okafor, Calvert-Lewin, Bahoya

Daniel Farke believes Leeds can go far in the Carabao Cup this year 💪 pic.twitter.com/26ueAAUHoZ

On the Brazilian winger’s opportunity tonight, Hasselbaink said on Sky Sports: “He has to find his place. This is his opportunity... It’s not really an out-and-out left-wing [position] or a No 10 as he can play, but [with] good players it doesn’t matter where you put them on the pitch. He will find his spaces and he will be direct as he was when he came in against Arsenal. He is going to play for his place because he wants to play week-in, week-out.”

"He deserves to be there because of what he has shown" Xabi Alonso speaks about Reggie Watson with the 16-year-old set to make his Chelsea debut in their Carabao Cup game against Leeds 🌟 pic.twitter.com/AAn4Av3iEh

Tfl has closed South Kensington station after a “customer incident” meaning parts of the District Line have closed. The decision was then made to delay the match to give supporters more time to get to the stadium.

Reggie Watson will become the fourth youngest player, aged 16, in Chelsea’s history. But he will have to wait a little bit longer for his debut as kick-off has been delayed by 15 minutes to 8.15pm.

There will be a 15 minute delay to kick-off for our Carabao Cup third round tie with Leeds United tonight. The match will now begin at 20:15 BST. pic.twitter.com/MdDXpxgW09

A couple of cracking strikes from the Dutchman. Some player he was...

"Good old days!" Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink reflects on his goals for Leeds against Chelsea 🎞️ pic.twitter.com/bYjyFYIVIK

LeedsAug 22: Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds 1Aug 25: Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds 2Aug 30: Leeds 1 Brentford 1Sep 5: Brighton 1 Leeds 1

As recently as March, a giant mural of Estêvão Willian appeared on the side of a building outside Stamford Bridge as the teenager threatened to become Chelsea’s number one poster boy.

He may no longer hold top billing outside the club, following a summer in which Chelsea spent a club-record £117m on Morgan Rogers to complete a fearsome front three alongside Cole Palmer and João Pedro.

A giant mural of the Brazilian teenager appeared on the side of a building close to Stamford Bridge in March.

But inside Stamford Bridge, nothing has changed. Estêvão remains one of Chelsea’s star boys and is part of an “untouchable” group of players that also includes Palmer, Rogers and Pedro. Sources believe Estêvão is a player the club will look at rewarding with an improved contract in the coming months.

Having already earned his Chelsea “untouchable” status, the next challenge for the 19-year-old winger – once nicknamed “Messinho” – is to make himself undroppable.

Estêvão may not be a perfect fit for Xabi Alonso’s three-at-the-back formation that features two 10s – Palmer and Rogers – behind a striker. But the boy from Brazil is certainly not being squeezed out and Chelsea’s manager has spoken of the need to be flexible.

Chelsea Penders; Gusto, Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill, Chavarria; Watson, Barco; Estevao, Gittens; Welbeck

Substitutes Martinez, Hato, Fofana, James, Neto, Palmer, Quenda, Rogers, Pedro

Leeds United Zetterer; Justin, Bijol, Muharemovic; James, Ampadu, Longstaff, Bard; Wilson, Aaronson; Nmecha

Substitutes Trafford, Gudmundsson, Elvedi, Bogle, Tanaka, Stach, Okafor, Calvert-Lewin, Bahoya

Much has been made of Chelsea’s willingness to let the opposition have the ball under Xabi Alonso, but tonight they will likely be forced to dictate proceedings. In Leeds, they face one of only two sides who have completed fewer passes than them in the Premier League.

1. Ian Hamilton in 1967: 16 years, four months and 15 days2. Kingsley Whiffen in 1967: 16 years, five months and six days3. Reggie Walsh in 2025: 16 years, six months and 11 days4. Reggie Watson in 2026: 16 years, seven months and 14 days5. Tommy Langley in 1974: 16 years, nine months and one day

Asked how he will approach the Carabao Cup this season, Daniel Farke said: “We’ll try to win it. That’s the quickest way to Europe and to some glory. Of course knowing that the Premier League will always have the priority and knowing that we are as successful as possible there, especially to reach our first goal to establish ourselves [at] this level.

“We are not the favourites to win the Carabao Cup, we know this. Challenging, difficult games, but of course we travel to London in order to go through in the next round without doing anything stupid at this stage of the campaign because you also have to rotate a bit more and integrate a few new players. Nevertheless, we want to be at our best and anyhow possible we also want to go through to the next round.”

Tonight represents an opportunity for 16-year-old Reggie Watson to announce himself at senior level. The central-midfielder caught Alonso’s eye during pre-season when the Spaniard said of him: “Reggie Watson, a great midfielder. He thinks, he’s very collective, he’s very generous on the effort, intelligent with the ball”.

“For his age, I’m really impressed with him.”

Dan James passes a late fitness test to make Daniel Farke’s starting XI.

📋 Tonight's Starting XI pic.twitter.com/MQKQtGZm8c

Reggie Watson, 16, son of former Wigan midfielder Ben (of 2013 FA Cup final fame), makes his full Chelsea debut and becomes the club’s fourth youngest player. Estevao, Jamie Gittens and Danny Welbeck replace Alonso’s thrilling forward three, who are on the bench.

Chelsea XI Penders; Gusto, Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill, Chavarria; Watson, Barco; Estevao, Gittens; Welbeck

Your Blues to face Leeds United in the #CarabaoCup! #CFC pic.twitter.com/636SOiUXVB

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of tonight’s Carabao Cup third-round tie between Chelsea and Leeds United. This is a rematch of last season’s FA Cup semi-final which Chelsea edged by a single Enzo Fernández goal, but plenty has changed since then. Xabi Alonso has taken over the reins at Stamford Bridge and made a promising start, reeling off three wins before losing to Arsenal in an absorbing contest last Sunday. Chelsea are not involved in European competition this season, so the domestic cups represent an avenue to silverware, as well as an opportunity to tinker.

In Alonso’s way, though, stands a Leeds team whose manager, Daniel Farke, told the media on Tuesday that his side are aiming to win the Carabao Cup. Farke has overseen an impressive run of form, having lost only two of their previous 16 competitive matches in a stretch that extends back to March. Two wins at Nottingham Forest preceded draws against Brentford and Brighton to keep Leeds undefeated this term. Farke has suggested he will rotate in west London to “integrate new players” having brought in seven new recruits during the summer.

If Leeds are to reach the next round, they must reverse a heavily one-sided head-to-head record against their hosts, who have won each of their past 10 cup meetings (three in the League Cup, seven in the FA Cup). In fact, Chelsea have lost at this stage of the competition just once in the past 15 years, and that was against Pep Guardiola’s Manchester City four seasons ago.

Alonso broke up the exhilarating “JP Morgan” band (João Pedro, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers) for Chelsea’s victory over Luton Town in the previous round, handing starts to Danny Welbeck and Estêvão. Players such as Jamie Gittens and Geovany Quenda are also waiting in the wings and may get chances to impress tonight. Mike Penders could also be in line for a start between the sticks.

#1815. A potential audition and the scorers from midfield: The five key battles in Milan vs. Frosinone

AC Milan resume their Serie A campaign after the final international break on 2026 by welcoming Frosinone to San Siro.

Ruben Amorim’s side are in need of a win to climb back into the top four after Como’s result on Saturday, while Roma and Lazio also picked up victories. They face a Frosinone team who will be full of confidence after an excellent start to their campaign, following promotion in 2025-26.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The latest team news suggests that Amorim will go with a 4-4-1-1 formation, though in his pre-match press conference he did not give too much away about his selection choices, especially in view of Thursday’s trip to Greece.

At the risk of sounding like a broken record, something simply has to click for Goncalo Ramos, and preferably soon. He has gone one month without a goal and his struggles to even generate shots followed him to Portugal on international duty. However, Frosinone are a side that score goals but also let them in too, so there should be spaces to exploit.

It will be an intriguing battle between the No.9 and Gabriele Calvani, while it could even be an audition of sorts for the centre-back. Milan have been linked with the Genoa loanee, who has made an impressive start to the campaign, so it will be an up-close look as he tries to pile the misery on Ramos.

With top scorer Antonio Raimondo out injured, Giorgi Kvernadze will be the main goal threat for the away side. The Georgian’s seven goal contributions are only bettered by the Italian striker, and he has started all 11 games under Alvini so far in Serie A.

It seems that Mario Gila will be tasked with stopping Kvernadze. The Spaniard spent the break at Milanello after not being called up by Spain again, and he should slot in as the right-sided defender again next to Koni De Winter.

Moving into midfield, there will be a fascinating contest between Adrien Rabiot and Giacomo Calo. It starts with a very obvious point of comparison: both are known for their goal scoring prowess, with the Frenchman already on five for the season and the Italian having racked up the same number.

The pair are likely to face each other head-to-head too. Whereas Rabiot has usually played deeper like Calo, it seems that the head coach is thinking of moving him further forward to play behind Ramos, so he will see a lot of Calo and also Patrizio Masini.

Alvini is expected to give the nod to Aleksa Terzic at left-back, which is notable because the Serbian has only started one game so far in 2026-27, with his other four appearances all coming off the bench. He does like to get forward in transition though, and has a goal to his name.

Primarily, Terzic will be tasked with trying to limit Diego Moreira’s impact on the game. The Belgian – who scored for his national team for the first time in their rout of Italy – is expected to start on the right for the Rossoneri, and his seven goal contributions in seven games tell their own story.

Finally, we return to the middle of the park where Luka Modric and Romano Schmid will headline as series of interesting duels. Modric’s importance to Milan in all phases of the game have been written about at length, but particularly the build-up phase in games where his team are expected to dominate the ball.

The Croatian is the metronome for the Rossoneri just as the summer signing Schmid is for the Canarini. The Austrian has been playing mostly as an attacking midfielder, with two goals and four assists to his name, and starts in all 11 rounds thus far.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has warned Ethan Nwaneri that brief flashes of quality will not be enough to secure regular football at Borussia Dortmund.

The record-breaking 19-year-old joined the Bundesliga leaders on loan from the Gunners in the summer, but has struggled for opportunities in recent weeks.

Nwaneri could now face his parent club in Tuesday's Champions League meeting in north London, with Arteta making his expectations clear.

Nwaneri initially enjoyed opportunities in Niko Kovac's starting lineup after arriving in Germany, but his involvement has since diminished significantly.

The versatile attacking midfielder has not started a match in over a month and has played just five minutes across Dortmund's last three Bundesliga fixtures.

Arteta believes the teenager must show greater consistency to establish himself at the highest level, insisting that occasional impressive performances are not enough.

"We're talking here about the highest level in Europe," the Arsenal boss said (via the Evening Standard). "You can just shine in moments, but moments are not enough. Now you need to show the consistency."

The Spaniard also stressed that Nwaneri must earn his place in a talented Dortmund squad, rather than expect opportunities because of his Arsenal background.

"He needs to earn the right to play," Arteta added, explaining that joining a major European club does not automatically guarantee minutes.

Arteta remains convinced that Nwaneri has the mentality and quality to succeed, but acknowledged that his loan spells at Marseille and Dortmund form part of a challenging development journey.

Arsenal are understood to have the option to recall the youngster in January if his situation does not improve, with Arteta currently unconvinced that the Dortmund move is delivering the desired benefits.

Nwaneri is eligible to feature against his parent club on Tuesday, although Dortmund's strong form makes a starting place appear unlikely.

Nevertheless, the opportunity to face Arsenal off the bench could provide the teenager with an ideal platform to respond to Arteta's comments, particularly after his recent lack of involvement.

The Gunners boss has challenged him to show consistency and earn his place, rather than rely on occasional moments of quality. A positive contribution against the Premier League champions would certainly help his case.

Should Nwaneri find the net, he could join a select group of players to score against their parent clubs while on loan, including James Rodriguez against Real Madrid and Philippe Coutinho against Barcelona during their respective spells at Bayern Munich.

It would be a significant way to make his mark, although simply earning meaningful minutes against Arsenal would represent an encouraging step in his Dortmund journey.

#1811. Doncaster Rovers v Huddersfield Town: Martin Drury on away transformation as hosts eye more derby comforts

One of the most uplifting facets of Martin Drury's full-time tenure has been the transformation so far in 2026-27.

A good barometer of their improvement arrives in tonight's Yorkshire derby at Doncaster Rovers - on an evening when three points would see the Terriers move level on points with leaders Stockport County.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

A poor night at the South Yorkshire venue in February saw Town lose 1-0 in a toothless and tepid showing which received jeers from travelling fans at half-time and the final whistle.

It was one a number of bad days on the road. Others were played out at Oakwell, Valley Parade and further afield at Adams Park and Home Park.

There were plenty more too, especially in the second half of the season when the entertainment value was lamentably low.

In the away table in 25-26, Huddersfield were ranked a below-par 13th, with 25 points from 23 games. Refreshingly, the picture is changing, not just in terms of points ratio, but goals and chance creation.

Town have averaged two points a game on the road so far, with 14 points from their seven matches. It's currently the second best record in the division, factoring in goal difference.

Drury observed: "There was some criticism of the away form last season. Obviously, I came in February. Between February and the end of the season, the away form wasn't brilliant.

"Prior to that, for the seven months before that, there weren't enough points picked up on the road. And if you want to be successful, you need to do that.

"So that was certainly an area that we addressed in the summer. And we did some things around that with the players, both on and off the grass, around certain scenarios and places that you're going to go to and how we might play when we're home and away. I think the players have been brilliant.

"I think we're fourth or third best in the league, maybe, for away form at the current time.

"We're going to lose some games away. That's going to happen. But I have to say, the things that we wanted to try and learn from last season and get better at, the players have done really, really well with that.

"And we've gone to some tough places so far with different types of challenges that we've enjoyed and embraced."

Town face a Rovers side who don't usually mind derbies. They excelled, certainly in the first half, of the home game with Sheffield Wednesday last month and showed character to come from behind to secure a hard-earned stoppage-time point at Bradford City on Saturday.

The latter derby marked the first-team return of ex-Terriers defender Matty Pearson after almost two-and-a-half months out with injury.

Pearson came through the weekend draw, while Jamie Sterry, James Husband and Tommi O’Reilly are all in contention for tonight's game.

Eager to make up for lost time, Pearson commented: "It's one of those things, you feel helpless when you're injured. It's been a tough few months but I'm well past that now.

"It's how you handle things and react. I think everyone's career has ups and downs and it's how you bounce back and how you react to them situations."

Pearson unquestionably had a mixed time during his four seasons at Huddersfield.

The Keighley-born player continued: "It was a big change really. We had an unbelievable first season (2021-22) and got into the play-offs and final (against Nottingham Forest at Wembley).

"And then it was 'sliding doors'. I don't know the full ins and outs but we struggled for the following two or three seasons after that. We went from playoffs to relegation battles every season.

"It's hard to say exactly what went on, it's one of those where it's been taken over now and they look like they're having a good season so far."

While Town have incentives this evening, so do Rovers; victory would see them move out of the relegation zone and jump up three places to 18th.

Drury added: "They obviously scored late on Saturday, which gives them a little bit of a boost when they get a goal to draw the game.

"I'm sure they've wanted to pick up more points than they have done this season, but I think they're a team with energy and players that want to get on the ball and play and take the ball under pressure.

"They're a team that have scored a lot of goals from set-pieces and scored goals from transition, so they can attack fast.

"But for all the stats, there's also a lot of things where we feel we can impose ourselves and really hurt them. We're in a good place."

Star Town winger Derensili Sanches Fernandes is available for tonight's game, despite coming off with a slight foot issue/cramp on Saturday's loss to Leicester City. David Kasumu and Samson Tovide are sidelined.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

A gutsy late derby point at Bradford City, last time out, was also welcome, even if McCann has not been spared criticism from supporters in recent times, particularly following atrocious losses at MK Dons and Kidderminster Harriers.

Sharp, 40, who left Rovers at the end of last season - hitting a hat-trick in his final game in May—said: "I think Grant's showed his pedigree with two promotions from League Two and League One.

"He'll be chomping at the bit trying to get up the table because he's an ambitious manager who wants promotion, which is no different to what I would be.

"I think it's tough because he believes a lot in the players and I think it needs to rub off on the players.

"He always used to say it to me and the group: 'don't let me believe in you as much as you believe in each other'. And I think that may be the difference at the minute.

"I think some of the players need to step up a little bit more. I'm not going to name names, but they'll know who they are. They've got to all start pulling in the right direction and getting that club moving up the table."

Despite a difficult season so far for Rovers, boardroom support for McCann appears solid and unwavering - with the Northern Irishman having a strong working relationship with owner Terry Bramall and chief executive officer Gavin Baldwin.

Sharp, at Doncaster Sports College earlier this week as part of the EFL's Power of 72 campaign that celebrates the work that clubs and their charities do in the local community, continued: "I think (most) managers are three losses away from being under pressure. I think that's how it is in this day and age; you don't get the time.

"Managers are always asking for time. But I think if you don't win games, you're always under pressure as the media are on your back and fans.

"Ultimately, if that's happening, some of the players might turn on you. So the most important thing is the players and keeping them happy, especially the ones who aren't in the team, because you always need them throughout the season.

"Having as much good noise as you can have in your dressing room and your club fends off the media and all the negative noise surrounding it.

"If you can keep it out when it isn't going great - it’s probably not going as great as Grant and Doncaster would like at the minute - (that's good).

"But I know that he's got full backing of the board and the players. It's about building (on pitch) momentum. And I think that's something that Doncaster have really struggled with. They win a game, then lose two. That's why they are where they are at the minute."
