#1685. Spurs finally score... but still lose

They scored. Would you believe it? Tottenham Hotspur, the team with more zeroes than an England Ashes batting collapse, found the back of the net but still frustration persists for Roberto De Zerbi.

It could have been something different. The sight of the Italian dashing down the touchline in hailstones, grabbing his head in disbelief in the final seconds, showed this was not a straightforward tale of misery but, ultimately, the misery endures.

“I think this is five or six games we have been for sure not lucky,” De Zerbi lamented, but sympathy did not extend too far. Liverpool deservedly moved into the next round of the Carabao Cup, the gloss on Andoni Iraola’s most enjoyable night provided by Dominik Szoboszlai’s goal-of-the-season contender.

THAT'S MAGNIFICENT! 💥🔴Outrageous strike from Dominik Szoboszlai 👏👏👏 pic.twitter.com/meQ7nilsz6

Liverpool were abject against Fulham on Saturday but with 10 changes to the starting line-up, infused with the exuberance of novices Rio Ngumoha and the terrific Lewis Koumas, Iraola’s team were invigorated and only a lapse of concentration enabled Tottenham to make a fist of it.

Yes, they went down swinging, as their noisy fans demanded. But carelessness cannot be excused and while De Zerbi complained about bad luck, a bad miss from Lucas Bergvall in the 10th minute was the fork in the road for the tie. Tottenham stalled and Liverpool never looked back.

“We have to shoot more times and we have to shoot better,” De Zerbi harrumphed. “We have to finish better the clear situations. We are sorry for the result, disappointed and frustrated. I think it was unfair but we have to be stronger in these unlucky moments.”

Rather than fizzing his drive into the net, Bergvall succeeded only in firing straight at Giorgi Mamardashvili, when he had the whole target in front of him. It was, in all fairness, a brilliant save but he should never have been allowed to make it.

Big save from Giorgi Mamardashvili! 💪Lucas Bergvall is denied by the Liverpool goalkeeper. pic.twitter.com/fKUbfGLMku

The miss changed the atmosphere, as suddenly Liverpool grasped the need to be competitive. At the heart of it all were Ngumoha, James McConnell, Trey Nyoni and Koumas, the last-named a nuisance to Tottenham’s defenders in the way a wasp is to picnickers on a summer’s afternoon.

For all the money that has been lavished by this club over the past 14 months, the one thing that the locals buy into more than anything is the basics done properly: hard work, tackling, a refusal to take second best. Iraola did not want Koumas to go anywhere this summer and it was obvious why.

“I see him training every day,” Iraola said. “He knows very clearly what he needs to do, what the team needs. And also the energy he shows is contagious for the rest. When you see the runs up front, giving everything, you are kind of forced to go behind and use the same intensity levels.”

Simple tenacity enabled Liverpool to get back on an even keel and laid the foundation for them to take the lead. It was a terrific goal, started with a raking pass from Joe Gomez that Cody Gakpo controlled instantly on his chest before scuttling inside and inviting Ngumoha to charge forward.

Whether it was the winger or Destiny Udogie, who was sliding to make a challenge, that ended up playing the ball to Alexis Mac Allister is immaterial, all that mattered is that the Argentine effortlessly placed his shot into the top corner, leaving Martin Dubravka planted and helpless.

Pick that out!! 🇦🇷Alexis Mac Allister hits a beauty into the roof of the net 🔴 pic.twitter.com/G7OT27CA8P

Is Mac Allister playing with a point to prove? Possibly, given his comments about not being offered a new contract last week. Will Iraola be bothered? Not in the slightest. All he wants is top players at the top of their game and Mac Allister is climbing towards the levels he showed two years ago.

What De Zerbi would do to have a player in such form, but Tottenham are a skittish bunch, not the type of team who respond well in the face of adversity and their head coach, dressed in black with his oversized white trainers, regularly shook his head in exasperation.

His mood was not helped just before the interval, when Mohammed Kudus blasted over from eight yards following a zipped-in cross from Udogie, but he would not have called it truthfully if he had suggested Tottenham deserved parity at that stage. Soon Liverpool’s advantage would be doubled.

The buffer they sought arrived in the 54th minute and, again, it was another genuinely attractive goal, with possession being kept until it sped up when Ngumoha scurried forward, found Milos Kerkez, who played it to Mac Allister, who in turn gave Gakpo the opening he craved.

His touch was excellent, his finish was even better and away in the distance Iraola rattled his fists in delight. That is two goals and four assists to start the campaign for the Dutchman and yet Liverpool were ready to sell him to Manchester City two weeks ago. What on earth were they thinking?

Ruthless!! 🔥Cody Gakpo doubles Liverpool's lead against Spurs 🔴 pic.twitter.com/qlaaynMuwM

From that point, it seemed inconceivable that Liverpool would finish living on their nerves, but De Zerbi’s decision to introduce Andy Robertson – given a hero’s reception on his first return to Anfield – and Mateus Fernandes wrestled back some impetus. There was also a significant helping hand.

Unsurprisingly, Andy Robertson gets a great reception from the Liverpool fans on his return to Anfield 👏 pic.twitter.com/uNM6A00k5F

Mamardashvili had made some important saves, including one from Kudus that he celebrated on his own, but he is vulnerable at set-pieces and Fernandes’s looping corner gave Conor Gallagher the easiest headed opportunity in three years to change the dynamic.

Spurs have scored! ⚪️Conor Gallagher brings Roberto De Zerbi's side back into the game! pic.twitter.com/52zSCqClw4

“We were under pressure at the end, but I don’t think we were nervous,” Gakpo said.

He was right. Try as they might, Spurs could not quite get the opening they needed and as they chased in vain, Szoboszlai administered the final blow in mesmerising fashion, thrashing a bouncing ball into the Kop net from 30 yards. And as De Zerbi realised in the sodden conditions, with Tottenham it never rains. It only pours.

Tottenham Hotspur did not pay Roberto De Zerbi, their head coach, a survival bonus for keeping the club in the Premier League and now Spurs are saving a fortune on goal bonuses.

De Zerbi’s team are yet to score against Premier League opposition this season and face Liverpool in the third round of the Carabao Cup at Anfield on Tuesday night.

Our team to take on Tottenham Hotspur 🔴 pic.twitter.com/tZSJkPpH3y

A place in the League Cup fourth round is at stake at Anfield as Liverpool host Tottenham in an all-Premier League tie.

Liverpool were frustrated on the weekend, being held to a 0-0 draw at home against Fulham, meaning they have one win and three draws from their opening four league games.

“I am very happy with the squad,” Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola said. “I value a lot my players, if we win games, the squad will look amazing and fantastic, if we do not there is going to be a problem with the depth. I think we will see also tomorrow [tonight] players we have not seen still and I am really looking forward to seeing. I feel they are going to play well and help us and they still have not had their chance. You can decide and put the same players in every game. The problem is there will be a moment when they are really tired. And there is more risk of injury.

“But that is why we cannot say it does not work for anyone. There are players who play every three days with no issues. They are very robust, their performances do not change too much. There are other players where the risk is bigger and the performances are different. I have to learn who is ready to play games every three days and who needs a rest so their performance level is not affected. I thought I had it quite clear in my mind with some, but with others, it is new, even for them, because they have not played as many games. We are learning.”

Liverpool were knocked out in the fourth round of this competition last season, losing 3-0 at home against Crystal Palace. Joe Gomez returns to the squad for the hosts tonight after an injury early in pre-season but Giovanni Leoni, Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Federico Chiesa remain out.

Tottenham are still without a league win or goal this season. Their 0-0 draw at home against Everton Saturday means they sit just above the relegation zone. Tottenham overcame Charlton in the second round, convincingly winning 5-1 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last month.

“I think we are working well,” Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi said. “We played 30 minutes, 25 minutes very well [against Everton]. In that moment we could score two goals. Then we lost maybe the confidence because we did not score. For sure we have to improve. For sure I have big confidence in my players, they are very good players.

“We have to improve, yes. We can say the coach has responsibility if we do not score, yes, I accept, no problem. We did not win any game so far, yes. We are disappointed, sorry for that. But we have other positive things, like I said we did not [concede goals] in the last two games and the things we have to improve, we start our work. Nothing changed in my project and my idea.”

Tottenham’s League Cup journey last season came to an end in the fourth round last season, losing 2-0 at Newcastle. Sandro Tonali and Pedro Porro will not be involved tonight for the visitors and neither will Richarlison, who has been left out. Andrew Robertson returns to Anfield for the first time after leaving Liverpool in the summer following nine years on Merseyside.

Team news from Anfield to follow shortly.

#1684. Liverpool injury update: Andoni Iraola makes worrying Ryan Gravenberch admission - "Not in a good place"

By Ben Knapton | 24 Nov 2026 17:13, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 17:13

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has dropped a worrying admission over Ryan Gravenberch's fitness ahead of Wednesday's Champions League clash with Club Brugge.

The Dutchman has missed each of the Reds' last three games with a heel fracture and was unsurprisingly not included in Liverpool's 22-man squad for the trip to the Jan Breydel Stadion.

Gravenberch had returned to training before Liverpool's 4-0 win over Manchester United in Sunday's Premier League affair, but the former Ajax man is still no closer to a competitive comeback.

After landing in Belgium, Iraola fielded questions from the media in his pre-game press conference, and he admitted that Gravenberch's injury was proving more complex to solve than initially anticipated.

"With Ryan, it's a bit more difficult," Iraola said. "He's having pain, the things in the fascia are difficult to solve. Sometimes he's managing the pain, but now he's not in a good place. Let's see if we can find ways to solve the problem but they are injuries that are not easy to solve normally."

While the exact nature and severity of Gravenberch's injury is not entirely clear, the Netherlands international may be suffering from Plantar fasciitis, which would fit Iraola's description.

An inflammation of the heel, Plantar fasciitis can take anywhere between four and 12 weeks to get better, and Gravenberch has already been out since the beginning of November.

As a result, the Dutchman may be missing until the end of January in the worst-case scenario, meaning he would firstly miss matches against Chelsea, Tottenham Hotspur, Porto and Aston Villa before the end of the year.

Liverpool then face Manchester United, Inter Milan and Everton again in the early weeks of 2027, and it remains to be seen if Gravenberch's complex issue has settled down by then.

The 24-year-old has set up one goal in 12 appearances for Liverpool so far this season, and in his absence, Alexis Mac Allister, Trey Nyoni, Dominik Szoboszlai and James McConnell will be competing for midfield minutes.

As well as delivering a negative update on Gravenberch, Iraola also revealed that Cody Gakpo would likely miss the weekend's Merseyside derby with Everton too.

The attacker hurt his calf while representing the Netherlands during the international break, although Iraola has insisted that his issue is not severe.

"With Cody, it's a soleus injury," Iraola added. "It's not big but we expect he'll be out for the weekend. But it's more predictable."

Giovanni Leoni (knee), Conor Bradley (knee) and Hugo Ekitike (Achilles) are also on the sidelines for Liverpool, who sit eighth in the Champions League league-phase table with nine points from their opening four fixtures.

#1683. Cisse discusses desire to add assists, not even being at 50% and why he must thank Gabbia

Alphadjo Cisse has revealed that he would like to add more assists to his game, as well as why he has Matteo Gabbia to thank above all.

Milan put on a ruthless display at San Siro on Sunday night, beating Frosinone 5-1 to move back into the top four. Calvani’s own-goal started the rout, while Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari and Christian Pulisic all scored.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Cisse got his name on the scoresheet again just minutes after coming on, netting his ninth goal of the season. Diego Moreira set him up with a nice through ball in transition, and though the offside flag went up initially, VAR overturned it to award the goal.

After the game, Cisse spoke to both Sky and DAZN to give his thoughts on what was another very positive night for him personally and for the team. His comments are via MilanNews.

“I definitely always try to contribute in all positions, and I definitely prefer to play in my own position, but I’m always available in all roles. Which position? I won’t say (laughs).”

Where can you still grow and what does Amorim ask of you?

“I have to improve in many other areas. As always, scoring is always great. I’d also like to add a few assists for some of my team-mates, but the most important thing was always to bring home three points, and today we did that.”

Is there a team-mate you have to thank in particular?

“I definitely think Gabbia, because I was initially coming from Serie B, and settling into that kind of environment is never easy. But I had teammates who welcomed me very well, him especially, so for me everything was much easier.”

We also see you as a possible centre-forward…

“I’ll tell you the truth, come on, I’ll tell you. I prefer to play in the attacking midfield because, as I’ve always done, I always want to try to make plays, to entertain people. But maybe, who knows, I’ll also play as a striker, I don’t know. Let’s see…”

“At first I thought it was. Then, as they were checking it a bit, I thought it wasn’t.”

You’re Milan’s top scorer. Will we see a bicycle kick soon?

“The overhead kick used to be my specialty, but now it’s not. Let’s hope it happens. It’s always a great feeling to score, I want to add a few assists too. The important thing was the three points, and we got them.”

How far along are you in your development?

“Right now, I’m not even halfway there. Maybe even lower. There’s still a lot of work to do to get there. But I’m in the right place, and hopefully we can get there.”

Have you ever thought about what would have happened if you had gone to PSV?

“Better not to think about it. Let’s just say that I’ve always made the right decisions with my family, and thanks go to them, to the coach, to my team-mates, and I’m in the right place and on the right path.”

“Progress is the right word, because we’ve changed coaches, and it’s never easy. We’re a great team, with many champions. We still have a lot of work to do. Milan always has our backs, and that’s very important to me.”

#1682. Mikel Arteta clamps down on Arsenal stars' use of Fantasy Premier League after Christos Tzolis 'leaked' team news in his side 'Tzatziki FC' before Gunners beat Liverpool

Published: 08:39 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 07:02 EST, 21 November 2026

Mikel Arteta has clamped down on Arsenal stars' Fantasy Premier League (FPL) exploits after 'Tzatziki FC', Christos Tzolis' team, 'leaked' team news.

The Arsenal manager admitted he has 'taken measures' to ensure opponents are not given an advantage by his players' selections on the popular game.

Tzolis picked himself as captain of his FPL side prior to the Gunners' 1-0 victory over Liverpool, a clear indication that he would start after recently coming back from injury.

Arteta then caught wind of the situation and Tzolis removed all Arsenal players from his fantasy team for their next game against Hull.

X account FPL Focal identified 'Tzatziki FC' as the Greek winger's team and screenshots of his teams from both game weeks showed how his picks changed.

On Friday, speaking about this issue, Arteta said: 'With Christos, with the squad and with my kids as well. Constantly they are asking me about line-ups as well, because they want to know.

Christos Tzolis picked himself in Fantasy Premier League before starting the Liverpool game

Tzolis' team, seen here before the Liverpool clash, is called 'Tzatziki FC' and was identified as his side by X account FPL Focal

'It’s a topic, you know. These are the kind of things that are happening in our society right now and it’s something new.

'We haven’t dealt with it [before] and we need to put new things in place. Obviously confidentiality is something critical because it’s about trust and about what you are trying to do and that should be kept as a huge secret. We’ll take measures to make sure it doesn’t happen.'

Arteta then confirmed that those measures had already been taken.

Tzolis is a known obsessive of the game, which puts him among 13 million other players who participate every year.

He even quipped after providing an assist against Coventry earlier in the season: 'I will take the three points', referring to the FPL score for doing so.

Chelsea had a similar issue this season, with their players indicating that Joao Pedro was out injured, removing the Brazilian from their FPL teams before his absence was confirmed by the club.

Teams are taking the matter seriously and are keen to ensure any possible advantage their opponents might have regarding team news is nipped in the bud.

Five years ago, Aston Villa stopped their players from participating in FPL after a number of them took Jack Grealish out of their line-ups, notifying eagle-eyed competitors that he was injured.

Mikel Arteta has cracked down on FPL use and 'taken measures' to ensure there are no leaks

The potential impact of players joining the global GTA 6 mania is another concern for Arteta, with a number of top-flight players already sharing how gripped they will be by the new game.

Bryan Mbeumo posted the loading screen at midnight on Thursday, indicating that he was having a late-night gaming session just days before the Liverpool clash, while Alexander Isak has said he will be hunkering down to play the game.

Declan Rice has previously spoken about how he often games into the early hours after matches when adrenaline is still coursing through him.

And his manager noted: 'We’ll try to find out how much exposure we have to these kinds of games and make sure it’s the right one to be able to perform and focus on what we have to do.'

#1680. Liverpool’s attack beginning to click after win over Club Brugge, says Isak

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Alexander Isak believes Liverpool's "dangerous" attack is beginning to click after following up their win over Manchester United by beating Club Brugge in the Champions League.

Liverpool boosted their hopes of a top-eight finish with a 3-0 win at Jan Breydelstadion on Wednesday, with Isak netting either side of Florian Wirtz's superb 79th-minute finish.

Isak opened the scoring in the 13th minute, finishing after being teed up by Dominik Szoboszlai following Yann Sommer's sloppy pass that gifted Liverpool possession.

The Reds navigated a wave of Brugge pressure and put the game out of sight thanks to two late goals, with Wirtz scoring the first with a brilliant shot from just outside the penalty area.

Alisson then pumped a long ball forward for Isak to chase, with the Swede getting the better of Brandon Mechele before dinking the ball over Sommer and into the net.

Liverpool have now won consecutive matches by 3+ goals (4-0 v Man Utd and 3-0 v Brugge) for the first time since January (6-0 v Qarabag and 4-1 v Newcastle United).

Among all Premier League players, Isak has scored the joint-most away goals across all competitions this season (eight – level with Erling Haaland).

Bradley Barcola failed to register a goal involvement but looked dangerous, while Wirtz has now scored in three consecutive appearances for the first time as a Liverpool player, and for the first time overall at club level since September 2024 for Bayer Leverkusen (three).

"Perfect away win, I would say. The performance until we got the second one was never obvious which way it would go," Isak told TNT Sports.

"They put on a good game. We spoke about having to get the second goal. They were playing man-on-man, so I was against the defender the whole game.

"It's always difficult to say exactly where you are and how good you are, but I can say I'm in a good place and the team is in a good place, most importantly.

"Hopefully, it gets better from here. The attack in general is beginning to click. We have a lot of different combinations, and whoever comes in, we have a dangerous attack."

6 – Alexander Isak has scored in six consecutive away appearances for Liverpool. In the Premier League era, the only other player to do so in 6+ consecutive away outings for the Reds is Mo Salah (7 – August-October 2021). Delivering. https://t.co/lXKfG9aLZH

Liverpool's win saw them move onto 12 points and fifth in the 36-team standings, with games against Porto, Inter and Lens remaining in the league phase of the competition.

But, more importantly, Liverpool were able to register their first clean sheet in the Champions League in 2026-27, with Alisson making five saves to keep Brugge at bay.

In fact, Brugge were held goalless in the Champions League for the first time in 2026. In their first eight matches in the competition this year, they netted 22 goals at an average of 2.75 per game, but they could not find a way past Liverpool.

In his 18th game in charge, Liverpool have kept back-to-back clean sheets under Iraola for the first time, with the Spaniard thrilled by his team's defensive display.

"It was a very important game for us. It was a key moment to put us in a good position," Iraola said.

"We are guaranteed to be qualified for the knockouts, but now we want top eight. It was a more difficult game than it looks now after the result.

"It was difficult to expect; it would be a very open game, they would man-to-man mark. Big merit in keeping the clean sheet. Overall, it is a very good performance."

#1679. Plenty of praise rightly distributed: Player ratings for Milan-Frosinone from Italian papers

Several AC Milan players have been highly praised by the Italian media after the 5-1 dismantling of Frosinone at San Siro.

Milan ended up with goals from five different sources as Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all netted, in addition to the opening goal which was an own-goal by Calvani. Adrien Rabiot got three assists, while Diego Moreira shone too.

It was a statement result and a ruthless display of the weapons that the Rossoneri have in transition, and it moves Ruben Amorim’s side back into the top four, while they remain five points off leaders Lazio.

Starting with La Gazzetta dello Sport, they gave the team’s overall performance a score of 8 out of 10, which is the same mark that they gave Amorim for his selections and tactical handling of what could have been a tough game on paper.

Rabiot was the Serie A Man of the Match and he gets the crown from La Gazzetta too, scoring an 8. The worst performer was Davide Bartesaghi, who struggled in his battle with Ghedjemis and got a 5.5.

Moreira matched Rabiot with an 8, while Pulisic and Luka Modric were given a 7.5. Four players scored a 7: Yunus Musah, Ramos, Jashari and Cisse. Sankhoun Diawara (6.5) passed the test, with Koni De Winter, Strahinja Pavlovic and Pervis Estupinan being given a 6.

Corriere dello Sport were a tad harsher with their scoring, giving Rabiot a 7.5 as the highest score. Jashari, Moreira, Modric, Pulisic and Ramos were handed a 7. They gave Cisse a 6.5, and everyone else got a passing score. Amorim (7.5) was also praised.

Tuttosport meanwhile gave Rabiot an 8, distributing 7.5s instead to Moreira, Modric, Pulisic and the coach Amorim. Scores of 7 went to Jashari, Musah, Ramos and Cisse. Gila, De Winter and Diawara got given a 6.5, and everyone else a 6.

#1678. Sporting Lisbon vs. Man United: Red Devils head coach Mauricio Pochettino handed much-needed boost for Champions League showdown

By Matt Law | 24 Nov 2026 18:27, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 18:29

Manchester United have been boosted by the return of Luke Shaw for Wednesday's Champions League clash with Portuguese giants Sporting Lisbon.

Shaw has not featured for Man United since October 10 due to a muscular problem, but he returned to training ahead of the European match and has been named in the travelling squad.

The Englishman's return is major news for the Red Devils given their defensive problems, but it remains to be seen whether he is considered for a start on Wednesday.

Matheus Cunha is a notable absentee through suspension, with the Brazil international sent off in the team's last match in the competition against Roma.

Meanwhile, Carlos Baleba, Marcus Rashford and Benjamin Sesko remain sidelined alongside long-term absentee Manuel Ugarte.

Man United have six points to show from their four matches in the competition, which has left them in 18th in the overall table.

Head coach Mauricio Pochettino has major decisions to make when it comes to his defensive unit for this match, as Matthijs de Ligt struggled in the 4-0 loss to Liverpool last time out.

Leny Yoro had been facing a Premier League suspension, increasing his chances of being involved from the first whistle against Sporting.

However, Yoro's red card against Liverpool has been overturned following a successful appeal.

The 21-year-old will therefore now be available to face Brentford at Old Trafford on Sunday.

Karl Darlow has also returned to the squad for the Sporting trip, having recovered from the injury that forced him to miss out against Liverpool.

Forwards: Amad, Shea Lacey, Bryan Mbeumo, Joshua Zirkzee

#1677. Jashari delighted after ‘beautiful’ Frosinone win and first Milan goal: “I promised the fans”

Ardon Jashari claims he promised the AC Milan fans he would score, so he was happy to deliver on his promise.

Milan put on a counter-attacking clinic at San Siro on Sunday night against Frosinone, winning 5-1. An own-goal from Gabriele Calvani kicked things off, with Goncalo Ramos, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic also netting.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

There was a special moment for Jashari just after coming on at half-time as he scored the third goal of the night and his first for the club. It came in transition, with the Swiss midfielder running in behind and thumping a powerful shot in off the near post, leaving the goalkeeper stunned.

Jashari spoke to SportMediaset after the final whistle at San Siro to reflect on what was a great night both for the team and for him on a personal note, with his words via MilanPress.

“Finally, I’m very happy with my first goal for Milan. It was a great feeling, and I’m happy for our team. We played a very intense, beautiful game against a tough and united team, both on and off the ball. We won, and we have to continue like this on Thursday, and for the rest of the season.”

“I hope so. I’m happy with today and I’ll try to continue like this for the team and the fans. It’s very important to have won.”

⚽️ GOAL ARDON JASHARI! His first for #ACMilan! 👏 https://t.co/fdfHgOJtfJ

— SempreMilan (@SempreMilanCom) November 22, 2026

What can you tell us about your position today?

“I played next to Luka today. Normally, strikers score goals, but today it was my turn. When I score, I score beautiful goals (smiles). It seemed like the goal against Venezia, but today it was even better because it was mine. The celebration was the same. I promised the fans I would score, and that’s what happened.”

“In my opinion, it’s very important to continue like this. The season is too long until May. Now it’s November. We’ve had a good season so far, but there are five months to go until May. We need these results against all our opponents. Today it was Frosinone, there’s still a lot to do.

“When you play for Milan, you have to win games and trophies, but it’s November. Everyone knows what it means to wear the Milan shirt, it’s important to continue like this. When you win, you’re good, when you lose, you’re not. It doesn’t matter who scores.”
